translations.literal: Treatise 57.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 57

sentences.zh: 禮一（

translations.literal: Rites 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Rites 1 (

sentences.zh: 吉禮一）

translations.literal: Auspicious Rites 1).
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious Rites 1)

sentences.zh: 自虞廷修五禮，兵休刑措。

translations.literal: From the time the court of Yu revised the Five Rites, arms were laid down and punishments set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the court of Yu codified the Five Rites, warfare ceased and punishments fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 天秩雖簡，鴻儀實容。

translations.literal: Though the heavenly order was simple, grand ceremony truly held all within it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's ordering may have been spare, yet majestic ritual truly embraced everything.

sentences.zh: 沿及漢、唐，訖乎有明，救敝興雅，咸依為的。

translations.literal: Extending through Han and Tang down to the Ming, remedying decadence and reviving elegance—all took this as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Tang through the Ming, every effort to cure decline and restore refinement took this as its touchstone.

sentences.zh: 煌煌乎，上下隆殺以節之，吉凶哀樂以文之，庄恭誠敬以贊之。

translations.literal: Splendid indeed: superior and inferior were regulated by degrees of elevation and abasement; auspice and misfortune, sorrow and joy were given ornament; solemnity, respect, sincerity, and reverence lent them support.
translations.idiomatic: How resplendent it was—rank and station measured by ritual gradation, fortune and grief, joy and mourning given their proper forms, and dignity, reverence, sincerity, and devotion lending the whole their force.

sentences.zh: 縱其間淳澆世殊，要莫不弘亮天功，雕刻人理，隨時以樹之范。

translations.literal: Though customs differed between pure and corrupt ages, in essence none failed to magnify heaven's work, carve out human principle, and erect standards suited to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Even when ages differed in innocence or decadence, each in its way exalted heaven's work, shaped human order, and set up models fit for its own time.

sentences.zh: 故群甿蒸蒸，必以得此而後足於憑依，洵品彙之璣衡也。

translations.literal: Thus the multitude, thriving together, could feel secure only once they possessed this—it was truly the balance-weight of all living kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the people, flourishing as one, found security only when they could rely on this—it was truly the standard by which all things were weighed.

sentences.zh: 斟之酌之，損之益之，修明而講貫之，安見不可與三代同風！

translations.literal: Measure it, temper it, trim and augment it, clarify and expound it—how could one say it could not share the same wind as the Three Dynasties!
translations.idiomatic: Refine it, adjust it, pare away and add to it, clarify and teach it through—and who is to say it cannot stand shoulder to shoulder with the Three Dynasties!

sentences.zh: 世祖入關，順命創製，規模閎遠。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor entered the Pass, he followed Heaven's mandate to establish institutions on a broad and far-reaching scale.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Emperor crossed into China proper, he obeyed Heaven's mandate to create institutions on a grand and far-sighted scale.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，詔禮臣參酌往制，勒成禮書，為民軌則。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, he ordered rites officials to consult past systems, compile them into a book of rites, and make it a standard for the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3, he commanded rites officials to weigh past regulations, fix them in a ritual code, and make that code the people's guide.

sentences.zh: 聖祖歲御經筵，纂成日講禮記解義，敷陳雖出群工，闡繹悉遵聖訓。

translations.literal: The Sage Emperor annually presided at the classics lecture; the Daily Lectures on the Meaning of the Book of Rites was compiled—though the exposition came from the assembled officials, the interpretation wholly followed the imperial instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Sage Emperor held the classics lecture every year and oversaw the Daily Lectures on the Meaning of the Book of Rites; though the lecturing fell to his ministers, every interpretation followed his teaching.

sentences.zh: 高宗御定三禮義疏，網羅議禮家言，折衷至當，雅號鉅制。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor personally fixed the Subcommentaries on the Meaning of the Three Rites, encompassing the sayings of ritual debaters and mediating them to the proper mean—elegantly hailed as a great compendium.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong Emperor personally approved the Subcommentaries on the Three Rites, gathering every school of ritual debate and reconciling them to the right mean—a work rightly praised as a monumental achievement.

sentences.zh: 若皇朝三通、大清會典，其經緯禮律，尤見本原。

translations.literal: As for the Three Comprehensive Statutes of the Dynasty and the Great Qing Collected Statutes, their weaving of ritual and law especially reveals the root origin.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's Three Comprehensive Statutes and the Great Qing Collected Statutes, in the way they interweave ritual and law, show the foundations especially clearly.

sentences.zh: 至於專書之最著者：一曰大清通禮，乾隆中撰成，道光年增修；

translations.literal: As for the most prominent specialized works: first, the Comprehensive Rites of the Great Qing, compiled in the Qianlong reign and revised in the Daoguang era;
translations.idiomatic: Among the most important specialized works, the first is the Comprehensive Rites of the Great Qing, drafted under Qianlong and revised in the Daoguang reign;

sentences.zh: 一曰皇朝禮器圖式，曰祭器、曰儀器、曰冠服、曰樂器、曰鹵簿、曰武備；

translations.literal: second, the Illustrated Forms of Ritual Implements of the Dynasty, covering sacrificial vessels, ceremonial implements, caps and robes, musical instruments, imperial regalia, and military equipment;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Illustrated Forms of Ritual Implements of the Dynasty, with sections on sacrificial vessels, ceremonial implements, caps and robes, musical instruments, imperial processional regalia, and military equipment;

sentences.zh: 一曰滿洲祭神祭天典禮，其始關外啟蓽，崇祭天神暨群祀祖禰，意示從儉。

translations.literal: third, the Manchu Rites for Sacrificing to Spirits and Heaven; at first, beyond the Pass when the enterprise was begun, they honored sacrifice to the Heavenly Spirit and collective worship of ancestors and forebears, the intent being to keep to frugality.
translations.idiomatic: third, the Manchu Rites for Sacrificing to Spirits and Heaven; in the earliest days beyond the Pass, when the enterprise was launched, they revered sacrifice to Heaven and collective worship of the ancestors, deliberately keeping the rites spare.

sentences.zh: 凡所紀錄，悉用國語、國書。

translations.literal: All that was recorded used entirely the national language and national script.
translations.idiomatic: Everything recorded was set down entirely in the national language and script.

sentences.zh: 入關後，有舉莫廢。

translations.literal: After entering the Pass, whatever observances existed were not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest, none of these observances was allowed to lapse.

sentences.zh: 逮高宗時，依據清文，譯成四卷。

translations.literal: By the Gaozong reign, on the basis of the Qing script, it was translated into four fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, it was translated into four fascicles on the basis of the Manchu text.

sentences.zh: 祭期、祭品、儀注、祝辭。

translations.literal: Sacrificial seasons, sacrificial offerings, ritual protocols, and prayer texts.
translations.idiomatic: It covers sacrificial seasons, offerings, ritual protocols, and prayer texts.

sentences.zh: 與夫口耳相傳，或小有異同者，並加釐訂，此國俗特殊之祀典也。

translations.literal: Together with what was transmitted by word of mouth, where there were slight differences, all were revised and corrected—this is a cult unique to national custom.
translations.idiomatic: Where oral tradition yielded slight variations, those too were corrected—making this a cult peculiar to the dynasty's own customs.

sentences.zh: 德宗季葉，設禮學館，博選耆儒，將有所綴述。

translations.literal: In the late years of the Dezong reign, a Hall of Ritual Learning was established, eminent Confucians broadly selected, intending to compile further works.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Dezong reign, a Hall of Ritual Learning was founded and eminent scholars chosen widely, with plans to compile new ritual texts.

sentences.zh: 大例主用通禮，仿江永禮書例，增曲禮一目。

translations.literal: The general plan chiefly used the Comprehensive Rites, following the model of Jiang Yong's Book of Rites and adding a section on the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The main framework was to follow the Comprehensive Rites, take Jiang Yong's Book of Rites as a model, and add a section on the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 又仿宋太常因革禮例，增廢禮、新禮二目，附後簡。

translations.literal: Again following the model of the Song Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Rites of Reform and Abolition, two sections on abolished rites and new rites were added, appended at the end in brief.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Song Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Rites of Reform and Abolition, they also added sections on abolished rites and new rites, appended briefly at the end.

sentences.zh: 未及編訂，而政變作矣。

translations.literal: Before compilation could be completed, political upheaval occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Before the work could be finished, political upheaval intervened.

sentences.zh: 其祀典之可稽者，初循明舊，稍稍褒益之。

translations.literal: As for the cult statutes that can be traced, at first they followed Ming precedents and were gradually elevated and augmented.
translations.idiomatic: Where the state cult can be traced, the dynasty at first followed Ming precedent and then gradually enlarged and enriched it.

sentences.zh: 堂子之祭，雖於古無徵，然昭假天神，實近類祀。

translations.literal: The Tangzi sacrifice, though without ancient precedent, in making manifest appeal to the Heavenly Spirit is in fact close to a category of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangzi sacrifice, though without ancient warrant, in its manifest appeal to Heaven is in substance very like a proper cult.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，以禁中祭上帝、大享殿合祀天地日月及群神、太廟階下合祭五祀非古制，詔除之。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign, because sacrifice to the Supreme Lord within the Forbidden City, the Great Offering Hall's joint sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, sun, moon, and the host of spirits, and the joint sacrifice to the Five Sacrifices below the steps of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were not ancient institutions, an edict abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, sacrifice to the Supreme Lord inside the Forbidden City, the Great Offering Hall's joint worship of Heaven, Earth, sun, moon, and all spirits, and the joint Five Sacrifices below the Imperial Ancestral Temple steps were judged uncanonical and abolished by edict.

sentences.zh: 又罷禘祭，專行祫祭。

translations.literal: The di sacrifice was also abolished, and only the xia sacrifice was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The di sacrifice was dropped as well, leaving only the xia seasonal offering.

sentences.zh: 高宗修雩祀，廢八蜡，建兩郊壇宇，定壇廟祭器，舉廢一惟其宜。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor restored the rain-prayer sacrifice, abolished the Eight La sacrifices, built the altars of the two suburbs, fixed the sacrificial vessels of altars and temples, and in every abolition or restoration acted only as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong restored the rain-prayer rite, abolished the Eight La sacrifices, built the suburban altars, standardized altar and temple vessels, and in every change did only what was appropriate.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遺命罷郊配祔廟，文宗限以五祖三宗，慮至深遠。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor's testamentary command abolished suburban accompaniment and enshrinement in the temple; the Wenzong Emperor limited it to five ancestors and three imperial forebears—forethought exceedingly far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong's deathbed command ended suburban accompaniment and temple enshrinement together; Wenzong limited the line to five ancestors and three imperial forebears—foresight of rare depth.

sentences.zh: 穆宗登遐，禮臣援奉先殿增龕座例，主升祔。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor passed away, rites officials cited the precedent of adding a niche in the Hall of Ancestral Veneration, and the late emperor was elevated and enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong died, rites officials cited the precedent of adding a niche in the Hall of Ancestral Veneration, and his spirit tablet was raised and enshrined.

sentences.zh: 議者病簡略，然亦迫於勢之不容已耳。

translations.literal: Critics faulted the brevity, yet they were also compelled by circumstances that brooked no delay.
translations.idiomatic: Critics complained of oversimplification, yet they were driven by circumstances that left no alternative.

sentences.zh: 光緒間，依高宗濮說辨，稱醇親王為本生考，立廟別邸，祀以天子禮。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign, following the Gaozong Emperor's Discourse on the Pu Temple, Prince Chun was styled the emperor's biological father, a separate temple and residence were established, and he was worshipped with the rites of a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu, following Gaozong's Discourse on the Pu Temple, Prince Chun was recognized as the emperor's biological father, given a separate temple and residence, and honored with imperial rites.

sentences.zh: 恩義兼盡，度越唐、明遠矣。

translations.literal: Favor and righteousness were both fully discharged, surpassing Tang and Ming by far.
translations.idiomatic: Grace and duty were both fulfilled to the full, far exceeding what Tang or Ming had done.

sentences.zh: 若夫郊廟大祀，無故不攝，誠敬仁孝，永垂家法，尤舉世所推。

translations.literal: As for the great suburban and temple sacrifices, without cause no proxy was appointed; sincerity, reverence, benevolence, and filial piety were forever handed down as household law—especially what the world commends.
translations.idiomatic: In the great suburban and temple sacrifices, no substitute was appointed without grave cause; sincerity, reverence, benevolence, and filial piety were enshrined as permanent household law—above all what the world most admires.

sentences.zh: 今為考諸成憲，循五禮序，條附支引，凡因襲變創，所以因時而制宜者，悉臚其要於編。

translations.literal: Now, examining the established statutes, following the order of the Five Rites, arranging items with branches and citations, whatever was inherited or newly created—whatever was adapted to the times—all essentials are set forth in this compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Here we examine the established statutes, follow the order of the Five Rites, arrange topics with cross-references, and set forth every essential point of what was inherited or newly devised to suit the times.

sentences.zh: 壇壝之制神位祭器祭品玉帛牲牢之數祀期齋戒祝版祭服祭告習儀陪祀

translations.literal: Regulations for altars and enclosures; spirit tablets; sacrificial vessels; offerings; jade and silk; victims; numbers of sacrifices; sacrificial seasons; fasting; prayer boards; sacrificial robes; announcements; rehearsal; attendant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Altars and enclosures; spirit tablets; sacrificial vessels and offerings; jade, silk, and victims; the schedule of sacrifices; fasting; prayer texts; vestments; proclamations; rehearsal; and attendant worship.

sentences.zh: 五禮，一曰吉禮。

translations.literal: Of the Five Rites, the first is auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Five Rites, the first is auspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 凡國家諸祀，皆屬於太常、光祿、鴻臚三寺，而綜於禮部。

translations.literal: All state sacrifices belong to the three directorates of Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Court of State Ceremonial, and are overseen by the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: All state sacrifices fall under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Court of State Ceremonial, with overall supervision by the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 惟堂子元日謁拜，立桿致祭，與內廷諸祀，並內務府司之。

translations.literal: Only the Tangzi New Year's audience, the raising of the pole for sacrifice, and the various inner-court sacrifices are administered by the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Tangzi New Year's audience, the raising of the sacrificial pole, and the various inner-court sacrifices are handled by the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 清初定制，凡祭三等：圜丘、方澤、祈穀、太廟、社稷為大祀。

translations.literal: In the early Qing fixed regulations, sacrifices were of three grades: the Circular Mound, Square Mound, Prayer for Grain, Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Altars of Soil and Grain were great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under early Qing regulations, sacrifices fell into three grades: the Circular Mound, Square Mound, Prayer for Grain, Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Altars of Soil and Grain ranked as great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天神、地祇、太歲、朝日、夕月、歷代帝王、先師、先農為中祀。

translations.literal: Heavenly spirits, earthly spirits, Grand Year Star, Morning Sun, Evening Moon, successive dynastic emperors, Former Teacher, and Former Farmer were medium sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly and earthly spirits, the Grand Year Star, Morning Sun and Evening Moon, successive dynastic emperors, the Former Teacher, and the Former Farmer ranked as medium sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 先醫等廟，賢良、昭忠等祠為群祀。

translations.literal: Temples such as the Former Physician, and shrines such as Worthy and Loyal and Manifest Loyalty were group sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Temples such as the Former Physician and shrines such as Worthy and Loyal and Manifest Loyalty ranked as group sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 乾隆時，改常雩為大祀，先蠶為中祀。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign, the regular rain-prayer sacrifice was changed to a great sacrifice, and the Former Silkworm to a medium sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, the regular rain-prayer rite was raised to a great sacrifice and the Former Silkworm to a medium sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 咸豐時，改關聖、文昌為中祀。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng reign, Guan the Sage and Wenchang were changed to medium sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianfeng, Guan the Sage and Wenchang were raised to medium sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 光緒末，改先師孔子為大祀，殊典也。

translations.literal: At the end of the Guangxu reign, the Former Teacher Confucius was changed to a great sacrifice—an extraordinary honor.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Guangxu, Confucius as Former Teacher was raised to a great sacrifice—an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 天子祭天地、宗廟、社稷。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven himself sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 有故，遣官告祭。

translations.literal: If there is cause, an official is dispatched to announce the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When prevented, he sends an official to announce the sacrifice in his stead.

sentences.zh: 中祀，或親祭、或遣官。

translations.literal: For medium sacrifices, he may sacrifice in person or dispatch an official.
translations.idiomatic: For medium sacrifices, he may attend in person or send an official.

sentences.zh: 群祀，則皆遣官。

translations.literal: For group sacrifices, officials are always dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: For group sacrifices, officials are always sent.

sentences.zh: 大祀十有三：正月上辛祈穀，孟夏常雩，冬至圜丘，皆祭昊天上帝；

translations.literal: Great sacrifices number thirteen: on the first xin day of the first month, Prayer for Grain; in the first month of summer, the regular rain prayer; at the winter solstice, the Circular Mound—all sacrifice to the August Heaven, Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: There are thirteen great sacrifices: Prayer for Grain on the first xin day of the first month, the regular rain prayer in early summer, and the Circular Mound at the winter solstice—all to the August Heaven, Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 夏至方澤祭皇地祇；

translations.literal: at the summer solstice, the Square Mound sacrifices to the August Earth, Imperial Earth Spirit;
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice, the Square Mound sacrifices to the August Earth, Imperial Earth Spirit;

sentences.zh: 四孟享太廟，歲暮祫祭；

translations.literal: in the four first months of the seasons, offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and at year's end the xia sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple in each season's first month, and the year-end xia sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 春、秋二仲，上戊，祭社稷；

translations.literal: in spring and autumn, on the second month's shangwu day, sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain;
translations.idiomatic: in spring and autumn, on the shangwu day of the second month, sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain;

sentences.zh: 上丁祭先師。

translations.literal: on the shangding day, sacrifice to the Former Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: and on the shangding day, sacrifice to the Former Teacher.

sentences.zh: 中祀十有二：春分朝日，秋分夕月，孟春、歲除前一日祭太歲、月將，春仲祭先農，季祭先蠶，春、秋仲月祭歷代帝王、關聖、文昌。

translations.literal: Medium sacrifices number twelve: at the spring equinox, audience with the sun; at the autumn equinox, evening audience with the moon; in early spring and the day before New Year's Eve, sacrifice to the Grand Year Star and the lunar generals; in mid-spring, sacrifice to the Former Farmer; in the last month of the season, sacrifice to the Former Silkworm; in the second months of spring and autumn, sacrifice to successive dynastic emperors, Guan the Sage, and Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: Medium sacrifices number twelve: the sun at the spring equinox and the moon at the autumn equinox; the Grand Year Star and lunar generals in early spring and on New Year's Eve; the Former Farmer in mid-spring and the Former Silkworm at season's end; and successive emperors, Guan the Sage, and Wenchang in the second month of spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 群祀五十有三：季夏祭火神，秋仲祭都城隍，季祭砲神。

translations.literal: Group sacrifices number fifty-three: in the last month of summer, sacrifice to the Fire Spirit; in mid-autumn, sacrifice to the metropolitan city god; in the last month of the season, sacrifice to the Cannon Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Group sacrifices number fifty-three: the Fire Spirit in late summer, the metropolitan city god in mid-autumn, and the Cannon Spirit at season's end.

sentences.zh: 春冬仲月祭先醫，春、秋仲月祭黑龍、白龍二潭暨各龍神，玉泉山、昆明湖河神廟、惠濟祠，暨賢良、昭忠、雙忠、獎忠、褒忠、顯忠、表忠、旌勇、睿忠親王、定南武壯王、二恪僖、弘毅文襄勤襄諸公等祠。

translations.literal: In the second months of spring and winter, sacrifice to the Former Physician; in the second months of spring and autumn, sacrifice at the Black Dragon and White Dragon pools and to the various dragon spirits, the Yuquan Mountain, Kunming Lake River Spirit Temple, and Huiji Shrine, and to shrines such as Worthy and Loyal, Manifest Loyalty, Paired Loyalty, Rewarding Loyalty, Commending Loyalty, Displaying Loyalty, Exemplifying Loyalty, Honoring Valor, Prince Rui the Loyal, the Dingnan Martial and Stalwart King, the two Ke and Xi, and the various lords Hongyi, Wenxiang, and Qinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second months of spring and winter, the Former Physician; in the second months of spring and autumn, the Black Dragon and White Dragon pools and all dragon spirits, the Yuquan Mountain, Kunming Lake River Spirit Temple, and Huiji Shrine, and shrines to Worthy and Loyal, Manifest Loyalty, Paired Loyalty, and the many other loyalty shrines, Prince Rui the Loyal, the Dingnan Martial and Stalwart King, the two Ke and Xi, and lords Hongyi, Wenxiang, and Qinxiang.

sentences.zh: 其北極佑聖真君、東嶽都城隍，萬壽節祭之。

translations.literal: The North Pole Savior Sage True Lord and the Eastern Peak metropolitan city god are sacrificed to on the Longevity Festival.
translations.idiomatic: The North Pole Savior Sage and the Eastern Peak metropolitan city god are worshipped on the Longevity Festival.

sentences.zh: 亦有因時特舉者，視學釋奠先師，獻功釋奠太學，御經筵祗告傳心殿。

translations.literal: There are also special observances according to occasion: inspecting studies and offering the libation to the Former Teacher, presenting achievements and offering the libation at the Imperial Academy, and at the classics lecture reverently announcing at the Hall of Transmitting the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Special observances also arise as occasion demands: inspecting studies and offering the libation to the Former Teacher, presenting military achievements at the Imperial Academy, and reverently announcing at the Hall of Transmitting the Heart during the classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 其岳、鎮、海、瀆，帝王陵廟，先師闕里，元聖周公廟，巡幸所蒞，或親祭，或否。

translations.literal: As for the peaks, garrisons, seas, and waterways, imperial tombs and temples, the Former Teacher's temple at Qufu, the Primordial Sage Duke of Zhou's temple—wherever the imperial tour arrives, he may sacrifice in person or not.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacred peaks, garrisons, seas, and waterways, imperial tombs and temples, Confucius's temple at Qufu, and the Duke of Zhou's temple, the emperor may sacrifice in person when his tour reaches them, or he may not.

sentences.zh: 遇大慶典，遣官致祭而已。

translations.literal: On great celebratory occasions, an official is merely dispatched to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On great celebratory occasions, an official is simply sent to perform the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 各省所祀，如社稷，先農，風雷，境內山川，城隍，厲壇，帝王陵寢，先師，關帝，文昌，名宦、賢良等祠，名臣、忠節專祠，以及為民御災捍患者，悉頒於有司，春秋歲薦。

translations.literal: What the provinces sacrifice to—such as the altars of soil and grain, Former Farmer, wind and thunder, mountains and rivers within the borders, city gods, plague altars, imperial tombs, Former Teacher, Lord Guan, Wenchang, shrines to eminent officials and worthy men, dedicated shrines to famous ministers and loyal martyrs, and those who warded off calamity and defended the people for the populace—all are promulgated to the responsible officials for spring and autumn annual offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial sacrifices—to soil and grain, the Former Farmer, wind and thunder, local mountains and rivers, city gods, plague altars, imperial tombs, the Former Teacher, Lord Guan, Wenchang, shrines to eminent officials and worthy men, martyrs' shrines, and protectors of the people—are all assigned to local officials for spring and autumn offerings.

sentences.zh: 至親王以下家廟，祭始封祖並高、曾、祖、禰五世。

translations.literal: As for family temples from princes downward, they sacrifice to the founder of the enfeoffment together with four generations of great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, and father—five generations.
translations.idiomatic: In family temples from princes downward, worship extends to the founding ancestor of the enfeoffment plus four generations—five generations in all.

sentences.zh: 品官逮士庶人祭高、曾、祖、禰四世。

translations.literal: Ranked officials down to commoners sacrifice to four generations: great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, and father.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials down to commoners worship four generations of ancestors.

sentences.zh: 其餘或因事，或從俗，第無悖於祀典，亦在所不禁。

translations.literal: The rest, whether arising from particular events or following local custom, so long as they do not violate the cult statutes, are also not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Other observances, whether occasioned by events or local custom, are permitted so long as they do not violate the cult statutes.

sentences.zh: 此其概也。

translations.literal: This is the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the general outline.

sentences.zh: 若夫壇壝神位，祭獻品物，齋戒告虔，及一切度數節文，詳其異同，識其顛末，無遺無複，庶覽者可考而知已。

translations.literal: As for altars and enclosures, spirit tablets, sacrificial offerings, fasting and reverent announcement, and all measures and ritual stages—detailing their differences and similarities, tracing their beginnings and ends, omitting nothing and repeating nothing—so that readers may examine and know.
translations.idiomatic: As for altars, spirit tablets, offerings, fasting, and every measure and ritual detail, we set forth differences and similarities, trace each matter from beginning to end, omit nothing and repeat nothing, so that readers may consult and understand.

sentences.zh: 壇壝之制天聰十年，度地盛京，建圜丘、方澤壇，祭告天地，改元崇德。

translations.literal: Regulations for altars and enclosures: In the tenth year of Tiancong, land was measured at Shengjing, the Circular Mound and Square Mound altars were built, Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to and announced, and the reign title was changed to Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: Altars and enclosures: In Tiancong 10, land was surveyed at Shengjing, the Circular Mound and Square Mound altars were built, Heaven and Earth were worshipped and announced, and the reign title was changed to Chongde.

sentences.zh: 天壇制圓，三成，上成九重，周一丈八尺；

translations.literal: The Heaven Altar was round, of three tiers; the upper tier had nine layers, with a circumference of one zhang eight chi;
translations.idiomatic: The Heaven Altar was circular, in three tiers; the upper tier had nine layers and a circumference of one zhang eight chi;

sentences.zh: 二成七重，周三丈六尺；

translations.literal: the second tier seven layers, circumference three zhang six chi;
translations.idiomatic: the second tier seven layers, circumference three zhang six chi;

sentences.zh: 三成五重，周五丈四尺：俱高三尺。

translations.literal: the third tier five layers, circumference five zhang four chi—all three tiers three chi high.
translations.idiomatic: the third tier five layers, circumference five zhang four chi—each tier three chi high.

sentences.zh: 垣周百十有三丈。

translations.literal: The enclosing wall had a circumference of one hundred thirteen zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The enclosing wall measured one hundred thirteen zhang in circumference.

sentences.zh: 地壇制方，二成，上成方六丈，高二尺；

translations.literal: The Earth Altar was square, of two tiers; the upper tier was six zhang square, two chi high;
translations.idiomatic: The Earth Altar was square, in two tiers; the upper tier was six zhang square and two chi high;

sentences.zh: 下成方八丈，高二尺四寸。

translations.literal: the lower tier eight zhang square, two chi four cun high.
translations.idiomatic: the lower tier eight zhang square and two chi four cun high.

sentences.zh: 垣周百三十有三丈。

translations.literal: The enclosing wall had a circumference of one hundred thirty-three zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Its enclosing wall measured one hundred thirty-three zhang in circumference.

sentences.zh: 制甚簡也。

translations.literal: The design was very simple.
translations.idiomatic: The design was very spare.

sentences.zh: 世祖奠鼎燕京，建圜丘正陽門外南郊，方澤安定門外北郊，規制始拓。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor established the capital at Yanjing, he built the Circular Mound outside the Zhengyang Gate in the southern suburb and the Square Mound outside the Anding Gate in the northern suburb—the scale was first expanded.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Emperor fixed the capital at Yanjing, he built the Circular Mound outside the Zhengyang Gate in the southern suburb and the Square Mound outside the Anding Gate in the northern suburb—the scale was first enlarged.

sentences.zh: 圜丘南鄉，三成，上成廣五丈九尺，高九尺；

translations.literal: The Circular Mound faced south, with three tiers; the upper tier was five zhang nine chi wide, nine chi high;
translations.idiomatic: The Circular Mound faced south, in three tiers; the upper tier was five zhang nine chi across and nine chi high;

sentences.zh: 二成廣九丈，高八尺一寸；

translations.literal: the second tier nine zhang wide, eight chi one cun high;
translations.idiomatic: the second tier nine zhang across and eight chi one cun high;

sentences.zh: 三成廣十有二丈，高如二成。

translations.literal: the third tier twelve zhang wide, the same height as the second tier.
translations.idiomatic: the third tier twelve zhang across, the same height as the second.

sentences.zh: 甃磚合一九七五陽數。

translations.literal: The paving bricks totaled one nine seven five—the yang numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The paving bricks totaled 1,975—the yang numbers.

sentences.zh: 陛四齣，各九級。

translations.literal: There were four flights of steps, each of nine steps.
translations.idiomatic: Four flights of steps rose from it, each of nine steps.

sentences.zh: 欄楯柱覆青琉璃。

translations.literal: The balustrades, rails, and pillars were covered with blue glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: Balustrades, rails, and pillars were faced with blue glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 內壝圓，周九十七丈七尺五寸，高八尺一寸。

translations.literal: The inner enclosure was round, circumference ninety-seven zhang seven chi five cun, height eight chi one cun.
translations.idiomatic: The inner enclosure was circular, ninety-seven zhang seven chi five cun in circumference and eight chi one cun high.

sentences.zh: 四面門各三，門柱各二。

translations.literal: On all four sides there were three gates each, with two gate pillars each.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the four sides had three gates, each with two gate pillars.

sentences.zh: 燔柴爐、瘞坎各一。

translations.literal: There was one brazier for burning firewood and one burial pit for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: There was one brazier for burning firewood and one pit for burying offerings.

sentences.zh: 外壝方，周二百四丈八尺五寸，高九尺一寸。

translations.literal: The outer enclosure was square, circumference two hundred four zhang eight chi five cun, height nine chi one cun.
translations.idiomatic: The outer enclosure was square, two hundred four zhang eight chi five cun in circumference and nine chi one cun high.

sentences.zh: 四門如內壝。

translations.literal: The four gates were like those of the inner enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Its four gates matched those of the inner enclosure.

sentences.zh: 北門後為皇穹宇，南鄉，制圓。

translations.literal: Behind the north gate was the Imperial Vault of Heaven, facing south, round in form.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the north gate stood the Imperial Vault of Heaven, facing south in circular form.

sentences.zh: 八柱環轉，重檐金頂。

translations.literal: Eight pillars arranged in a ring, with double eaves and a gilded roof.
translations.idiomatic: Eight pillars ringed the hall, with double eaves and a gilded roof.

sentences.zh: 基周十三丈七寸，高九尺。

translations.literal: The platform was thirteen zhang seven cun in circumference, nine chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Its platform measured thirteen zhang seven cun around and nine chi high.

sentences.zh: 陛三出，級十有四。

translations.literal: Three flights of steps, fourteen steps each.
translations.idiomatic: Three flights of steps rose from it, each of fourteen steps.

sentences.zh: 左右廡各五楹，陛一出，七級。

translations.literal: On left and right, side halls of five bays each, with one flight of steps of seven steps.
translations.idiomatic: Side halls of five bays stood to left and right, each with a single flight of seven steps.

sentences.zh: 殿廡覆瓦俱青琉璃。

translations.literal: The hall and side halls were all roofed with blue glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: Hall and side halls alike were roofed with blue glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 圍垣周五十六丈六尺八寸，高丈有八寸。

translations.literal: The surrounding wall had a circumference of fifty-six zhang six chi eight cun, height one zhang eight cun.
translations.idiomatic: The surrounding wall measured fifty-six zhang six chi eight cun around and one zhang eight cun high.

sentences.zh: 南設三門。

translations.literal: On the south were set three gates.
translations.idiomatic: Three gates opened on the south.

sentences.zh: 外壝門外北神庫、神廚各五楹，南鄉。

translations.literal: Outside the outer enclosure gate, to the north were the Spirit Storehouse and Spirit Kitchen, five bays each, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: North of the outer enclosure gate stood the Spirit Storehouse and Spirit Kitchen, five bays each, facing south.

sentences.zh: 井亭一。

translations.literal: One well pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: There was one well pavilion.

sentences.zh: 其東為祭器、樂器、椶薦諸庫。

translations.literal: To the east were storehouses for sacrificial vessels, musical instruments, and palm mats.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lay storehouses for sacrificial vessels, musical instruments, and palm mats.

sentences.zh: 又東為井亭、宰牲亭。

translations.literal: Farther east were the well pavilion and the slaughter pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east stood the well pavilion and the slaughter pavilion.

sentences.zh: 壇內垣北圓，餘皆方。

translations.literal: Within the altar, the northern wall was round, the rest square.
translations.idiomatic: Within the altar precinct, the northern wall was circular and the rest square.

sentences.zh: 門四：東泰元，南昭亨，西廣利，北成貞。

translations.literal: Four gates: east Taiyuan, south Zhaohang, west Guangli, north Chengzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Four gates: east Taiyuan, south Zhaohang, west Guangli, north Chengzhen.

sentences.zh: 成貞北為大享殿。

translations.literal: North of Chengzhen was the Great Offering Hall.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Chengzhen gate stood the Great Offering Hall.

sentences.zh: 壇圓，南鄉。

translations.literal: The altar was round, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The altar was circular and faced south.

sentences.zh: 內外柱各十有二，中龍井柱四。

translations.literal: Inner and outer pillars twelve each, with four dragon-well pillars in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer rings each had twelve pillars, with four dragon-well pillars at the center.

sentences.zh: 金頂，檐三重，覆青、黃、綠三色琉璃。

translations.literal: Gilded roof, triple eaves, covered with blue, yellow, and green glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: It had a gilded roof and triple eaves roofed in blue, yellow, and green glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 基三成，南北陛三出，東西陛一出，上二成各九級，三成十級。

translations.literal: The platform had three tiers; on north and south three flights of steps, on east and west one flight; the upper two tiers nine steps each, the third tier ten steps.
translations.idiomatic: The platform had three tiers; north and south had three flights of steps, east and west one each; the upper two tiers had nine steps each and the third ten.

sentences.zh: 東西廡二重，前各九楹，後各七楹。

translations.literal: East and west side halls in two tiers, nine bays in front, seven bays behind each.
translations.idiomatic: East and west side halls stood in two tiers, nine bays in front and seven behind on each side.

sentences.zh: 前為大享門，上覆綠琉璃，前後三出陛，各十有一級。

translations.literal: In front was the Great Offering Gate, roofed with green glazed tile; front and back, three flights of steps, eleven steps each.
translations.idiomatic: Before it stood the Great Offering Gate, roofed in green glazed tile, with three flights of eleven steps front and back.

sentences.zh: 東南燔柴爐、瘞坎，制如圜丘。

translations.literal: Southeast were the firewood brazier and burial pit, of the same design as at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood the firewood brazier and burial pit, matching the Circular Mound in design.

sentences.zh: 內壝周百九十丈七尺二寸。

translations.literal: The inner enclosure measured one hundred ninety zhang seven chi two cun in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The inner enclosure measured one hundred ninety zhang seven chi two cun around.

sentences.zh: 門四，北門後為皇乾殿，南鄉，五楹，覆青琉璃。

translations.literal: Four gates; behind the north gate was the Imperial Qian Hall, facing south, five bays, roofed with blue glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: There were four gates; behind the north gate stood the Imperial Qian Hall, five bays facing south and roofed in blue glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 陛五齣，各九級。

translations.literal: Five flights of steps, nine steps each.
translations.idiomatic: Five flights of steps rose from it, each of nine steps.

sentences.zh: 東磚門外長廊七十二，聯檐通脊，北至神庫、井亭。

translations.literal: Outside the east brick gate were seventy-two long corridors, eaves joined in continuous ridge, extending north to the spirit storehouse and well pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the east brick gate ran seventy-two long corridors with joined eaves and continuous ridge, reaching north to the spirit storehouse and well pavilion.

sentences.zh: 又東北宰牲亭，薦俎時避雨雪處也。

translations.literal: Farther northeast was the slaughter pavilion, a shelter from rain and snow when presenting the offering trays.
translations.idiomatic: Farther northeast stood the slaughter pavilion, where attendants could shelter from rain and snow while preparing the offering trays.

sentences.zh: 壝外圍垣東、西、北各有門，南接成貞。

translations.literal: Outside the enclosure, the surrounding wall had gates on east, west, and north; on the south it joined Chengzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the enclosure, the surrounding wall had gates on the east, west, and north, and on the south joined the Chengzhen gate.

sentences.zh: 又西北曰齋宮，東鄉，正殿五楹，陛三出，中級十有三，左右各十五。

translations.literal: Farther northwest was the Fasting Palace, facing east; the main hall five bays, three flights of steps, the center flight thirteen steps, left and right fifteen each.
translations.idiomatic: Farther northwest stood the Fasting Palace, facing east; its main hall had five bays and three flights of steps—the center thirteen steps, the side flights fifteen each.

sentences.zh: 左設齋戒銅人，右設時辰牌。

translations.literal: On the left was set the bronze fasting figure; on the right, the time tablet.
translations.idiomatic: On the left stood the bronze fasting figure; on the right, the time tablet.

sentences.zh: 後殿五楹，左右配殿各三楹。

translations.literal: The rear hall five bays; left and right side halls three bays each.
translations.idiomatic: The rear hall had five bays, with side halls of three bays to left and right.

sentences.zh: 內宮牆方百三十三丈九尺四寸。

translations.literal: The inner palace wall was square, one hundred thirty-three zhang nine chi four cun.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace wall formed a square one hundred thirty-three zhang nine chi four cun on a side.

sentences.zh: 中三門，左右各一。

translations.literal: Three central gates, one each on left and right.
translations.idiomatic: There were three central gates and one each on the left and right.

sentences.zh: 環以池，跨石樑三。

translations.literal: It was encircled by a moat, crossed by three stone bridges.
translations.idiomatic: A moat encircled it, crossed by three stone bridges.

sentences.zh: 東北鐘樓一，外宮牆方百九十八丈二尺二寸，池梁如內製。

translations.literal: One bell tower to the northeast; the outer palace wall square, one hundred ninety-eight zhang two chi two cun; moat and bridges like the inner design.
translations.idiomatic: A bell tower stood to the northeast; the outer palace wall formed a square one hundred ninety-eight zhang two chi two cun on a side, with moat and bridges matching the inner design.

sentences.zh: 廣利門外西北為神樂觀，東鄉。

translations.literal: Northwest outside the Guangli Gate was the Temple of Divine Music, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest outside the Guangli Gate stood the Temple of Divine Music, facing east.

sentences.zh: 中凝禧殿，五楹。

translations.literal: In the center, the Ningxi Hall, five bays.
translations.idiomatic: At its center stood the Ningxi Hall of five bays.

sentences.zh: 後顯佑殿，七楹。

translations.literal: Behind, the Xianyou Hall, seven bays.
translations.idiomatic: Behind it stood the Xianyou Hall of seven bays.

sentences.zh: 西為犧牲所，南鄉。

translations.literal: To the west was the Victim Office, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stood the Victim Office, facing south.

sentences.zh: 又西為鐘樓，其大享殿圍垣南接圜丘，東、西轉北為圓形。

translations.literal: Farther west was the bell tower; the enclosing wall of the Great Offering Hall joined the Circular Mound on the south, turning north on east and west in a circular form.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west stood the bell tower; the Great Offering Hall's enclosing wall joined the Circular Mound on the south and curved north on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 內垣高一丈一尺，址厚九尺，頂厚七尺，周千二百八十六丈一尺五寸。

translations.literal: The inner wall was one zhang one chi high, nine chi thick at the base, seven chi at the top, circumference one thousand two hundred eighty-six zhang one chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The inner wall stood one zhang one chi high, nine chi thick at the base and seven at the top, with a circumference of one thousand two hundred eighty-six zhang one chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 外垣高一丈一尺五寸，址厚八尺，頂厚六尺，周千九百八十七丈五尺。

translations.literal: The outer wall one zhang one chi five cun high, eight chi thick at the base, six chi at the top, circumference one thousand nine hundred eighty-seven zhang five chi.
translations.idiomatic: The outer wall stood one zhang one chi five cun high, eight chi thick at the base and six at the top, with a circumference of one thousand nine hundred eighty-seven zhang five chi.

sentences.zh: 西鄉門二，南北並列焉。

translations.literal: Two gates facing west, aligned north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Two gates faced west, aligned north and south.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，修齋宮，改神樂觀為所。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong, the Fasting Palace was repaired and the Temple of Divine Music was changed to an office.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 8, the Fasting Palace was repaired and the Temple of Divine Music was redesignated an office.

sentences.zh: 十二年，修內外垣，改築圜丘，規制益拓。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, inner and outer walls were repaired and the Circular Mound rebuilt; the scale was further expanded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the inner and outer walls were repaired and the Circular Mound rebuilt on an even larger scale.

sentences.zh: 上成徑九丈，二成十五丈，三成二十一丈，一九三五三七，皆天數也。

translations.literal: The upper tier nine zhang in diameter, the second fifteen zhang, the third twenty-one zhang—one nine three five three seven—all heavenly numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier was nine zhang in diameter, the second fifteen, the third twenty-one—1, 9, 3, 5, 3, 7—all heavenly numbers.

sentences.zh: 通三成丈四十有五，符九五義。

translations.literal: The three tiers together forty-five zhang in height, matching the meaning of nine and five.
translations.idiomatic: The three tiers together stood forty-five zhang high, in keeping with the symbolism of nine and five.

sentences.zh: 量度准古尺，當營造尺八寸一分，又與九九數合。

translations.literal: Measurements followed the ancient foot, equivalent to eight cun one fen of the construction foot, again matching the number nine times nine.
translations.idiomatic: Measurements followed the ancient foot, equivalent to eight cun one fen of the construction foot, again matching nine times nine.

sentences.zh: 壇面甃磚九重，上成中心圓面，外環九重，磚數一九累至九九。

translations.literal: The altar surface was paved in nine layers of bricks; the upper tier had a circular center, nine rings outward, brick counts from one nine accumulating to nine nines.
translations.idiomatic: The altar surface was paved in nine layers of bricks; the upper tier had a circular center surrounded by nine rings, with brick counts rising from nineteen to eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 二三成以次遞加。

translations.literal: The second and third tiers increased in like manner by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The second and third tiers increased in the same manner by degrees.

sentences.zh: 上成每面各十有八，二成各二十七，三成各四十五，並積九為數，四乘之，綜三百有六十，以應周天之度。

translations.literal: The upper tier eighteen on each face, the second twenty-seven, the third forty-five—all accumulating nines, multiplied by four, totaling three hundred sixty, corresponding to the degrees of the celestial circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier had eighteen on each face, the second twenty-seven, the third forty-five—all built on nines, multiplied by four to total three hundred sixty, matching the degrees of the celestial circuit.

sentences.zh: 其高上成五尺七寸，二成五尺二寸，三成五尺。

translations.literal: Their heights: upper tier five chi seven cun, second five chi two cun, third five chi.
translations.idiomatic: Their heights were five chi seven cun for the upper tier, five chi two cun for the second, and five chi for the third.

sentences.zh: 欄、柱、階級並准今尺。

translations.literal: Balustrades, pillars, and steps all followed the present foot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Balustrades, pillars, and steps all followed the current foot measure.

sentences.zh: 古今尺度嬴縮稍差，用九則一。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern measures differed slightly in expansion and contraction; using nine, then one.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern measures differed slightly in scale; the design used nine, then one.

sentences.zh: 復改壇面為艾葉青石，皇穹宇檯面墁青白石，大享殿外壇面墁金磚。

translations.literal: The altar surface was again changed to mugwort-leaf green stone; the Imperial Vault of Heaven terrace was paved with blue-white stone; the Great Offering Hall outer altar surface was paved with golden bricks.
translations.idiomatic: The altar surface was repaved in mugwort-leaf green stone; the Imperial Vault of Heaven terrace in blue-white stone; and the Great Offering Hall's outer altar in golden bricks.

sentences.zh: 壇內殿宇門垣俱青琉璃。

translations.literal: Within the altar, halls, gates, and walls were all blue glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: Within the altar precinct, halls, gates, and walls were all faced in blue glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 十六年，更名大享殿曰祈年。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Great Offering Hall was renamed Prayer for the Year.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the Great Offering Hall was renamed the Hall of Prayer for the Year.

sentences.zh: 覆檐門廡壇內外壝垣並改青琉璃，距壇遠者如故。

translations.literal: Eaves, gates, side halls, and inner and outer enclosure walls within the altar were all changed to blue glazed tile; those far from the altar remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Eaves, gates, side halls, and inner and outer walls within the altar precinct were all changed to blue glazed tile; structures farther from the altar remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋增天壇外垣南門一，內垣鐘鼓樓一，嗣是祭天壇自新南門入，祭祈年殿仍自北門入。

translations.literal: Soon one south gate was added to the outer wall of the Heaven Altar and one bell-and-drum tower to the inner wall; thereafter sacrifice at the Heaven Altar entered by the new south gate, while sacrifice at the Prayer for the Year Hall still entered by the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a south gate was added to the Heaven Altar's outer wall and a bell-and-drum tower to the inner wall; thereafter Heaven Altar sacrifices entered by the new south gate, while Prayer for the Year Hall sacrifices still entered by the north gate.

sentences.zh: 二十年，改神樂所為署。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the Divine Music Office was changed to a directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, the Divine Music Office was redesignated a directorate.

sentences.zh: 五十年，重建祈穀壇配殿。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, the side halls of the Prayer for Grain Altar were rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, the side halls of the Prayer for Grain Altar were rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 光緒十五年，祈年殿災，營度仍循往制雲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu, the Prayer for the Year Hall suffered fire; reconstruction still followed the former design.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 15, the Hall of Prayer for the Year burned; reconstruction still followed the former design.

sentences.zh: 方澤北鄉，周四十九丈四尺四寸，深八尺六寸，寬六尺，祭日中貯水。

translations.literal: The Square Mound faced north; the moat forty-nine zhang four chi four cun in circumference, eight chi six cun deep, six chi wide; on the day of sacrifice water was stored in it.
translations.idiomatic: The Square Mound faced north; its moat measured forty-nine zhang four chi four cun around, eight chi six cun deep and six chi wide, and was filled with water on the day of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 二成，上成方六丈，二成方十丈六尺，合六八陰數。

translations.literal: Two tiers; the upper tier six zhang square, the second ten zhang six chi square—together the six-eight yin numbers.
translations.idiomatic: It had two tiers: the upper six zhang square and the second ten zhang six chi square—together the six-eight yin numbers.

sentences.zh: 壇面甃黃琉璃，每成陛四齣，俱八級。

translations.literal: The altar surface was paved with yellow glazed tile; each tier had four flights of steps, all of eight steps.
translations.idiomatic: The altar surface was paved in yellow glazed tile; each tier had four flights of eight steps.

sentences.zh: 二成南列岳鎮五陵山石座，鏤山形；

translations.literal: On the south of the second tier were arranged stone seats for the peaks, garrisons, and five imperial tombs, carved in mountain form;
translations.idiomatic: On the south of the second tier stood stone seats for the sacred peaks, garrisons, and five imperial tombs, carved in mountain form;

sentences.zh: 北列海瀆石座，鏤水形：俱東西鄉。

translations.literal: on the north, stone seats for the seas and waterways, carved in water form—all facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: On the north stood stone seats for the seas and waterways, carved in water form—all facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 內壝方二十七丈二尺，高六尺，厚二尺。

translations.literal: The inner enclosure was twenty-seven zhang two chi square, six chi high, two chi thick.
translations.idiomatic: The inner enclosure was twenty-seven zhang two chi square, six chi high and two chi thick.

sentences.zh: 正北門三，石柱六。

translations.literal: On the main north, three gates, six stone pillars.
translations.idiomatic: The main north had three gates and six stone pillars.

sentences.zh: 東、西、南門各一，石柱二。

translations.literal: East, west, and south one gate each, two stone pillars each.
translations.idiomatic: East, west, and south each had one gate and two stone pillars.

sentences.zh: 北門外西北瘞坎一。

translations.literal: Northwest outside the north gate, one burial pit.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest outside the north gate stood one burial pit.

sentences.zh: 外壝方四十二丈，高八尺，厚二尺四寸。

translations.literal: The outer enclosure forty-two zhang square, eight chi high, two chi four cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: The outer enclosure was forty-two zhang square, eight chi high and two chi four cun thick.

sentences.zh: 門制視內壝。

translations.literal: The gate design matched the inner enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: The gates matched those of the inner enclosure.

sentences.zh: 南門後皇祇室，五楹，北鄉。

translations.literal: Behind the south gate was the Imperial Earth Chamber, five bays, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the south gate stood the Imperial Earth Chamber, five bays facing north.

sentences.zh: 垣周四十四丈八尺，高一丈一尺。

translations.literal: The wall circumference forty-four zhang eight chi, height one zhang one chi.
translations.idiomatic: Its wall measured forty-four zhang eight chi around and one zhang one chi high.

sentences.zh: 正門一，外壝西門外，神庫，神廚，祭器、樂器諸庫，井亭，宰牲亭在焉。

translations.literal: One main gate; outside the west gate of the outer enclosure were the spirit storehouse, spirit kitchen, storehouses for sacrificial vessels and musical instruments, well pavilion, and slaughter pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: There was one main gate; outside the outer enclosure's west gate stood the spirit storehouse, spirit kitchen, storehouses for vessels and instruments, well pavilion, and slaughter pavilion.

sentences.zh: 西北曰齋宮，東鄉。

translations.literal: To the northwest was the Fasting Palace, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest stood the Fasting Palace, facing east.

sentences.zh: 正殿七楹，陛五齣，中九級，左右俱七級；

translations.literal: The main hall seven bays, five flights of steps, center nine steps, left and right seven each;
translations.idiomatic: The main hall had seven bays and five flights of steps—the center nine steps, the side flights seven each;

sentences.zh: 南北陛一出，各七級。

translations.literal: North and south one flight each, seven steps.
translations.idiomatic: North and south each had one flight of seven steps.

sentences.zh: 左右配殿各七楹。

translations.literal: Left and right side halls seven bays each.
translations.idiomatic: Side halls of seven bays stood to left and right.

sentences.zh: 宮牆周百有十丈二尺。

translations.literal: The palace wall circumference one hundred ten zhang two chi.
translations.idiomatic: The palace wall measured one hundred ten zhang two chi around.

sentences.zh: 門三，東鄉。

translations.literal: Three gates, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Three gates faced east.

sentences.zh: 東北鐘樓一，壇內垣周五百四十九丈四尺，北、西門各三，東、南門各一。

translations.literal: One bell tower to the northeast; the inner altar wall circumference five hundred forty-nine zhang four chi; north and west three gates each, east and south one each.
translations.idiomatic: A bell tower stood to the northeast; the inner altar wall measured five hundred forty-nine zhang four chi around, with three gates on the north and west and one each on the east and south.

sentences.zh: 外垣周七百六十五丈。

translations.literal: The outer wall circumference seven hundred sixty-five zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The outer wall measured seven hundred sixty-five zhang around.

sentences.zh: 西鄉門三。

translations.literal: Three gates facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Three gates faced west.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，重建齋宮，制如舊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, the Fasting Palace was rebuilt, the design as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8, the Fasting Palace was rebuilt to the former design.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，以皇祇室用綠瓦乖黃中制，諭北郊壇磚壝瓦改用黃。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, because the Imperial Earth Chamber used green tile contrary to the yellow-centered regulation, an edict ordered the northern suburban altar's brick enclosures and tiles changed to yellow.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 14, because the Imperial Earth Chamber used green tile contrary to the yellow-centered regulation, an edict ordered the northern suburban altar's brick walls and tiles changed to yellow.

sentences.zh: 明年，改築方澤墁石，壇面制視圜丘。

translations.literal: The following year, the Square Mound paving stones were rebuilt; the altar surface design followed the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the Square Mound was repaved, its altar surface following the Circular Mound in design.

sentences.zh: 上成石循前用六六陰數，縱橫各六，為三十六。

translations.literal: The upper tier stones followed the former use of the six-six yin numbers, six each in length and breadth, totaling thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier stones followed the six-six yin numbers, six in each direction for thirty-six in all.

sentences.zh: 其外四正四隅，均以八八積成，縱橫各二十四。

translations.literal: Outside, the four cardinal and four corner directions all accumulated by eight eights, twenty-four each in length and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them, the four cardinals and four corners were built up by eights, twenty-four in each direction.

sentences.zh: 二成倍上成，八方八八之數，半徑各八，為六八陰數，與地耦義符。

translations.literal: The second tier doubled the upper tier; in the eight directions the number eight-eight, half-diameter eight each—the six-eight yin numbers, matching the meaning of pairing with earth.
translations.idiomatic: The second tier doubled the upper; in the eight directions the eight-eight numbers, half-diameter eight each—the six-eight yin numbers, matching earth's paired symbolism.

sentences.zh: 尋建東、西、南壝門外南、北瘞坎各二。

translations.literal: Soon south and north burial pits, two each, were built outside the east, west, and south enclosure gates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two burial pits each were built south and north outside the east, west, and south enclosure gates.

sentences.zh: 又天、地二壇，立陪祀官拜石如其等。

translations.literal: Also at the Heaven and Earth altars, bowing stones for attendant-sacrifice officials were erected according to their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the Heaven and Earth altars, bowing stones for attendant officials were also erected according to rank.

sentences.zh: 闕右社稷壇，制方，北鄉。

translations.literal: To the right of the palace gate was the altars of soil and grain, square in form, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: To the right of the palace gate stood the altars of soil and grain, square in form and facing north.

sentences.zh: 二成，高四尺。

translations.literal: Two tiers, four chi high.
translations.idiomatic: It had two tiers, four chi high.

sentences.zh: 上成方五丈，二成方五丈三尺。

translations.literal: The upper tier five zhang square, the second five zhang three chi square.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier was five zhang square and the second five zhang three chi square.

sentences.zh: 陛四齣，各四級。

translations.literal: Four flights of steps, four steps each.
translations.idiomatic: Four flights of steps rose from it, each of four steps.

sentences.zh: 上成土五色，隨其方覆之。

translations.literal: The upper tier had soil of five colors, spread according to the direction.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier was covered with soil of five colors according to the directions.

sentences.zh: 內壝方七十六丈四尺，高四尺，厚二尺，飾色如其方。

translations.literal: The inner enclosure seventy-six zhang four chi square, four chi high, two chi thick, colored according to the direction.
translations.idiomatic: The inner enclosure was seventy-six zhang four chi square, four chi high and two chi thick, colored according to the directions.

sentences.zh: 門四，柱各二。

translations.literal: Four gates, two pillars each.
translations.idiomatic: There were four gates, each with two pillars.

sentences.zh: 壝西北瘞坎二。

translations.literal: Northwest of the enclosure, two burial pits.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of the enclosure stood two burial pits.

sentences.zh: 北拜殿，又北戟門，楹各五，陛三出。

translations.literal: To the north, the bowing hall; farther north, the halberd gate, five bays each, three flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: To the north stood the bowing hall; farther north, the halberd gate of five bays, with three flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 外列戟七十二，其西南神庫、神廚在焉。

translations.literal: Outside were arrayed seventy-two halberds; to the southwest were the spirit storehouse and spirit kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two halberds stood outside; to the southwest were the spirit storehouse and spirit kitchen.

sentences.zh: 壇垣周百五十三丈四尺，覆黃琉璃。

translations.literal: The altar wall circumference one hundred fifty-three zhang four chi, roofed with yellow glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: The altar wall measured one hundred fifty-three zhang four chi around and was roofed in yellow glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 北三門，東、西、南各一門。

translations.literal: Three gates on the north; east, west, and south one gate each.
translations.idiomatic: The north had three gates; east, west, and south one each.

sentences.zh: 西門外宰牲亭一、井一。

translations.literal: Outside the west gate, one slaughter pavilion and one well.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the west gate stood one slaughter pavilion and one well.

sentences.zh: 西南為奉祀署。

translations.literal: To the southwest was the Sacrificial Service Office.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest stood the Sacrificial Service Office.

sentences.zh: 壇東北正門一，左右門各一，俱東鄉，直闕右門，乘輿躬祭所出入也。

translations.literal: Northeast of the altar, one main gate, one gate each to left and right, all facing east, directly aligned with the right palace gate—the entry and exit for the imperial carriage when sacrificing in person.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of the altar stood one main gate and one each to left and right, all facing east and aligned with the right palace gate—the route by which the imperial carriage entered and left when the emperor sacrificed in person.

sentences.zh: 東南為社稷街。

translations.literal: To the southeast was the Street of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast lay the Street of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十一年，徙瘞坎壇外西北隅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Qianlong, the burial pits were moved to the northwest corner outside the altar enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 21, the burial pits were relocated to the northwest corner outside the altar enclosure.

sentences.zh: 舊制壝垣用五色土，至是改四色琉璃磚瓦。

translations.literal: Former regulations used five-colored earth for the enclosure walls; at this time they were changed to four-colored glazed brick and tile.
translations.idiomatic: Under the former regulations the enclosure walls used five-colored earth; at this point they were changed to four-colored glazed brick and tile.

sentences.zh: 及省社稷壇高二尺一寸，方廣二丈五尺，制殺京師十之五雲。

translations.literal: Provincial altars of soil and grain were two chi one cun high and two zhang five chi square, scaled to five-tenths of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial altars of soil and grain were two chi one cun high and two zhang five chi square—scaled to half the capital dimensions.

sentences.zh: 朝日壇在朝陽門外東郊，夕月壇在阜成門外西郊，俱順治八年建。

translations.literal: The Sun Altar was in the eastern suburb outside Chaoyang Gate; the Moon Altar in the western suburb outside Fucheng Gate—both built in the eighth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun Altar stood in the eastern suburb outside Chaoyang Gate and the Moon Altar in the western suburb outside Fucheng Gate; both were built in Shunzhi 8.

sentences.zh: 制方，一成，陛四齣。

translations.literal: Square in form, one tier, four flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: They were square in form, of one tier, with four flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 日壇各九級，方五丈，高五尺九寸。

translations.literal: The sun altar had nine steps on each flight, five zhang square, five chi nine cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The sun altar had nine steps on each flight, was five zhang square, and five chi nine cun high.

sentences.zh: 圓壝，周七十六丈五尺，高八尺一寸，厚二尺三寸。

translations.literal: Round inner enclosure, circumference seventy-six zhang five chi, eight chi one cun high, two chi three cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: The round inner enclosure measured seventy-six zhang five chi around, eight chi one cun high, and two chi three cun thick.

sentences.zh: 壇垣前方後圓，周二百九十丈五尺。

translations.literal: The altar wall was square in front and round behind, circumference two hundred ninety zhang five chi.
translations.idiomatic: The altar wall was square in front and round behind, two hundred ninety zhang five chi in circumference.

sentences.zh: 月壇各六級，方四丈，高四尺六寸。

translations.literal: The moon altar had six steps on each flight, four zhang square, four chi six cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The moon altar had six steps on each flight, was four zhang square, and four chi six cun high.

sentences.zh: 方壝，周九十四丈七尺，高八尺，厚二尺二寸。

translations.literal: Square inner enclosure, circumference ninety-four zhang seven chi, eight chi high, two chi two cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: The square inner enclosure measured ninety-four zhang seven chi around, eight chi high, and two chi two cun thick.

sentences.zh: 壇垣周二百三十五丈九尺五寸。

translations.literal: The altar wall circumference was two hundred thirty-five zhang nine chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The altar wall measured two hundred thirty-five zhang nine chi five cun around.

sentences.zh: 兩壇具服殿制同。

translations.literal: The robing halls of both altars shared the same design.
translations.idiomatic: The robing halls of both altars followed the same design.

sentences.zh: 燎爐，瘞坎，井亭，宰牲亭，神庫，神廚，祭器、樂器諸庫咸備。

translations.literal: Fire brazier, burial pits, well pavilion, slaughter pavilion, spirit storehouse, spirit kitchen, and all storehouses for sacrificial and musical implements were fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Fire braziers, burial pits, well pavilions, slaughter pavilions, spirit storehouses and kitchens, and all repositories for sacrificial and musical implements were fully provided.

sentences.zh: 其牌坊曰禮神街。

translations.literal: Its memorial archway was called Spirit-Rite Street.
translations.idiomatic: Its memorial archway was called Spirit-Rite Street.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，更名日壇街曰景升，月壇街曰光恆。

translations.literal: Early in Yongzheng, Sun Altar Street was renamed Jingsheng and Moon Altar Street Guangheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng, Sun Altar Street was renamed Jingsheng and Moon Altar Street Guangheng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十年，修建壇工，依天壇式。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Qianlong, altar construction followed the Temple of Heaven model.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 20, the altars were rebuilt on the model of the Temple of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 改內垣土牆甃以磚，其外垣增舊制三尺。

translations.literal: The inner earthen walls were faced with brick; the outer walls were raised three chi above the former standard.
translations.idiomatic: The inner earthen walls were faced with brick, and the outer walls were raised three chi above the former height.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，改日壇面紅琉璃，月壇面白琉璃，並覆金磚。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu period, the sun altar surface was changed to red glazed tile and the moon altar to white glazed tile, both paved with gold bricks.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu period, the sun altar surface was set in red glazed tile and the moon altar in white glazed tile, both paved with gold bricks.

sentences.zh: 天神、地祇、先農三壇制方，一成，陛皆四齣，在正陽門外。

translations.literal: The altars to Celestial Spirits, Terrestrial Spirits, and the Former Farmer were square, one tier, four flights of steps each, outside Zhengyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The altars to Celestial Spirits, Terrestrial Spirits, and the Former Farmer were square, of one tier, with four flights of steps each, and stood outside Zhengyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 先農壇位西南，周四丈七尺，高四尺五寸。

translations.literal: The Former Farmer altar stood southwest, circumference four zhang seven chi, height four chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Farmer altar stood in the southwest, four zhang seven chi around and four chi five cun high.

sentences.zh: 東南為觀耕台，耕耤時設之。

translations.literal: To the southeast was the terrace for observing the plowing; it was set up at the season of the plowing ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood the terrace for observing the plowing, erected for the plowing season.

sentences.zh: 前耤田，後具服殿。

translations.literal: Plowing fields in front, robing hall behind.
translations.idiomatic: Plowing fields lay in front and the robing hall behind.

sentences.zh: 東北神倉，中廩制圓。

translations.literal: Northeast was the spirit granary; the central granary was round in form.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast stood the spirit granary, with a round central storehouse.

sentences.zh: 前收穀亭，後祭器庫。

translations.literal: Grain-receiving pavilion in front, sacrificial vessels storehouse behind.
translations.idiomatic: A grain-receiving pavilion stood in front and a sacrificial vessels storehouse behind.

sentences.zh: 內垣南門外，神祇壇在焉。

translations.literal: Outside the south gate of the inner wall stood the altar of spirits and terrestrial forces.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the inner wall's south gate stood the altar of spirits and terrestrial forces.

sentences.zh: 神壇位東，方五丈，高四尺五寸五分。

translations.literal: The spirit altar stood east, five zhang square, four chi five cun five fen high.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit altar stood to the east, five zhang square and four chi five cun five fen high.

sentences.zh: 北石龕四，鏤雲形，分祀雲、雨、風、雷。

translations.literal: Four stone niches on the north, cloud patterns carved, separately worshipping cloud, rain, wind, and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the north were four stone niches carved with cloud patterns, for separate worship of cloud, rain, wind, and thunder.

sentences.zh: 祇壇位西，廣十丈，縱六丈，高四尺。

translations.literal: The terrestrial forces altar stood west, ten zhang wide, six zhang long, four chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The terrestrial forces altar stood to the west, ten zhang wide, six zhang long, and four chi high.

sentences.zh: 南石龕五，鏤山水形。

translations.literal: Five stone niches on the south, landscapes carved.
translations.idiomatic: On the south were five stone niches carved with landscapes.

sentences.zh: 分祀岳、鎮、海、瀆。

translations.literal: Separate worship for peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers were worshipped separately.

sentences.zh: 二壇方壝，俱周二十四丈，高五尺五寸。

translations.literal: Both altars had square inner enclosures, each twenty-four zhang in circumference, five chi five cun high.
translations.idiomatic: Both altars had square inner enclosures, each twenty-four zhang around and five chi five cun high.

sentences.zh: 正門分南、北，餘如日、月壇。

translations.literal: Main gates were divided north and south; the rest followed the sun and moon altars.
translations.idiomatic: The main gates were divided north and south; the rest followed the sun and moon altars.

sentences.zh: 又內垣東門外北齋宮，五楹，後殿，配殿，茶、膳房具焉。

translations.literal: Also north of the east gate outside the inner wall was the fasting palace—five bays, with rear hall, side halls, and tea and kitchen rooms complete.
translations.idiomatic: North of the east gate outside the inner wall stood the fasting palace of five bays, with rear hall, side halls, and tea and kitchen rooms.

sentences.zh: 乾隆時，更命齋宮曰慶成宮。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign, the fasting palace was renamed the Palace of Completed Felicity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, the fasting palace was renamed the Palace of Completed Felicity.

sentences.zh: 壇外垣周千三百六十八丈。

translations.literal: The outer wall circumference was one thousand three hundred sixty-eight zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The outer wall measured one thousand three hundred sixty-eight zhang around.

sentences.zh: 南、北門二，東鄉，南入先農壇，北入太歲殿。

translations.literal: Two gates north and south, facing east; the south led into the Former Farmer altar, the north into the Grand Year Hall.
translations.idiomatic: There were two gates north and south, both facing east: the south led into the Former Farmer altar and the north into the Grand Year Hall.

sentences.zh: 殿七楹，東、西廡各十有一。

translations.literal: The hall had seven bays; east and west corridors eleven each.
translations.idiomatic: The hall had seven bays, with eleven bays each in the east and west corridors.

sentences.zh: 其前曰拜殿，燎爐一。

translations.literal: Before it was the bowing hall, with one fire brazier.
translations.idiomatic: Before it stood the bowing hall, with one fire brazier.

sentences.zh: 先蠶壇，乾隆九年，建西苑東北隅，制視先農。

translations.literal: Former Silkworm altar: in the ninth year of Qianlong, built in the northeast corner of the Western Park, its design following the Former Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Silkworm altar was built in Qianlong 9 in the northeast corner of the Western Park, on the model of the Former Farmer altar.

sentences.zh: 徑四丈，高四尺，陛四齣。

translations.literal: Diameter four zhang, height four chi, four flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: It was four zhang in diameter, four chi high, with four flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 殿三楹，西鄉。

translations.literal: Hall three bays, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The hall had three bays and faced west.

sentences.zh: 東採桑台，廣三丈二尺，高四尺，陛三出。

translations.literal: East was the mulberry-picking terrace, three zhang two chi wide, four chi high, three flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: To the east stood the mulberry-picking terrace, three zhang two chi wide and four chi high, with three flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 前為桑園台，中為具服殿、為繭館，後為織室。

translations.literal: In front was the mulberry-garden terrace; in the middle the robing hall and cocoon hall; behind, the weaving room.
translations.idiomatic: In front lay the mulberry-garden terrace; in the middle were the robing hall and cocoon hall; behind stood the weaving room.

sentences.zh: 有配殿，環以宮牆。

translations.literal: Side halls were provided, enclosed by palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: Side halls were provided, enclosed within palace walls.

sentences.zh: 牆東浴蠶河，跨橋二。

translations.literal: East of the wall was the Silk-Bathing River, spanned by two bridges.
translations.idiomatic: East of the wall ran the Silk-Bathing River, crossed by two bridges.

sentences.zh: 橋東蠶署三，蠶室二十七，俱西鄉。

translations.literal: East of the bridges were three silkworm offices and twenty-seven silkworm chambers, all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: East of the bridges stood three silkworm offices and twenty-seven silkworm chambers, all facing west.

sentences.zh: 外垣周百六十丈，各省先農壇高廣視社稷，餘如制。

translations.literal: The outer wall measured one hundred sixty zhang around; provincial Former Farmer altars in height and breadth followed the soil and grain altars, the rest per regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The outer wall measured one hundred sixty zhang around; provincial Former Farmer altars matched the soil and grain altars in height and breadth, with the rest as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 神位、祭器、祭品、玉、帛、牲牢之數神位，圜丘第一成，正位昊天上帝，南鄉。

translations.literal: Counts of spirit positions, sacrificial vessels, offerings, jade, silks, and sacrificial animals—Spirit positions: at the Circular Mound first tier, the principal position was the August Heaven, Supreme Lord, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Counts of spirit positions, sacrificial vessels, offerings, jade, silks, and sacrificial animals. Spirit positions: at the Circular Mound's first tier, the principal August Heaven, Supreme Lord faced south.

sentences.zh: 配位八，首太祖訖宣宗，東西鄉。

translations.literal: Eight matching positions, from the Taizu Emperor through the Xuanzong Emperor, facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Eight matching positions ran from the Taizu Emperor through the Xuanzong Emperor, facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 凡位皆施幄。

translations.literal: Every position had canopy curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Every position was furnished with canopy curtains.

sentences.zh: 第二成從位，東大明，次星辰。

translations.literal: Second tier attendant positions: east, Great Brightness, then the stars.
translations.idiomatic: On the second tier, attendant positions to the east were Great Brightness, then the stars.

sentences.zh: 西夜明，次雲、雨、風、雷。

translations.literal: West, Night Brightness, then cloud, rain, wind, and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: To the west were Night Brightness, then cloud, rain, wind, and thunder.

sentences.zh: 常雩如冬至、大祀、大雩，有從無配。

translations.literal: The regular rain prayer, like the winter solstice, great sacrifice, and great rain prayer, had attendant positions but no matching positions.
translations.idiomatic: For the regular rain prayer, as for the winter solstice, great sacrifice, and great rain prayer, there were attendant positions but no matching positions.

sentences.zh: 祈穀位次視圜丘第一成，無幄。

translations.literal: Prayer for Grain positions ranked as the Circular Mound first tier, without canopies.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer for Grain positions followed the Circular Mound's first tier in rank, without canopies.

sentences.zh: 方澤第一成，正位皇地祇，北鄉，配列祖、列宗，東西鄉。

translations.literal: Square Mound first tier: principal position August Earth, Imperial Earth Spirit, facing north; successive ancestors and successive emperors matched, facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: At the Square Mound's first tier, the principal August Earth, Imperial Earth Spirit faced north, with successive ancestors and emperors matched to east and west.

sentences.zh: 第二成從位，東五嶽，啟運、隆業、永寧三山，次四海。

translations.literal: Second tier attendant positions: east, the Five Peaks, Qiyun, Longye, and Yongning three mountains, then the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: On the second tier, attendants to the east were the Five Peaks, the three mountains Qiyun, Longye, and Yongning, then the four seas.

sentences.zh: 西五鎮，天柱、昌瑞二山，次四瀆。

translations.literal: West, the Five Garrisons, Tianzhu and Changrui two mountains, then the four rivers.
translations.idiomatic: To the west were the Five Garrisons, the two mountains Tianzhu and Changrui, then the four rivers.

sentences.zh: 因事祗告天地，不設配從位。

translations.literal: When Heaven and Earth were respectfully notified on special occasions, no matching or attendant positions were set up.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven and Earth were notified on special occasions, no matching or attendant positions were established.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年，合祀大享殿，其正位左天帝，右地祇，南鄉。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi, worship was combined in the Hall of Grand Felicity; the principal positions had Heaven Lord on the left and Earth Spirit on the right, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17, worship was combined in the Hall of Grand Felicity, with Heaven Lord on the left and Earth Spirit on the right at the principal positions, facing south.
