sentences.zh: 東太祖，西太宗，配之。

translations.literal: East, Taizu; west, Taizong—as matching worship.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was matched to the east and Taizong to the west.

sentences.zh: 從祀十二壇，大明位東，星辰、五嶽、啟運、四海、太歲、名山大川次之。

translations.literal: Twelve attendant altars of worship: Great Brightness east; stars, Five Peaks, Qiyun, four seas, Grand Year, and famous mountains and great rivers followed.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve attendant altars of worship placed Great Brightness to the east, followed by the stars, Five Peaks, Qiyun, four seas, Grand Year, and famous mountains and great rivers.

sentences.zh: 夜明位西，雲、雨、風、雷、五鎮、天柱、隆業、四瀆、帝王、天下神祇次之。

translations.literal: Night Brightness west; cloud, rain, wind, thunder, Five Garrisons, Tianzhu, Longye, four rivers, emperors, and spirits of the realm under Heaven followed.
translations.idiomatic: Night Brightness stood to the west, followed by cloud, rain, wind, thunder, the Five Garrisons, Tianzhu, Longye, the four rivers, emperors, and spirits throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 社稷壇中植石主，別設神牌，正位。

translations.literal: At the soil and grain altar a stone lord was planted in the center; spirit tablets were set separately at the principal position.
translations.idiomatic: At the altars of soil and grain a stone lord was set in the center, with separate spirit tablets at the principal position.

sentences.zh: 東大社，西大稷。

translations.literal: East, Great Soil; west, Great Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Great Soil stood to the east and Great Grain to the west.

sentences.zh: 北鄉。

translations.literal: Facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Both faced north.

sentences.zh: 東配后土句龍氏，西后稷氏。

translations.literal: East matched Hou Tu Julong; west matched Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tu Julong was matched to the east and Hou Ji to the west.

sentences.zh: 無幄。

translations.literal: No canopies.
translations.idiomatic: There were no canopies.

sentences.zh: 壇下龕用木。

translations.literal: Niches below the altar were of wood.
translations.idiomatic: The niches below the altar were made of wood.

sentences.zh: 日壇東大明，無幄。

translations.literal: At the sun altar, Great Brightness east, without canopy.
translations.idiomatic: At the sun altar, Great Brightness stood to the east without a canopy.

sentences.zh: 月壇正位夜明，配北斗二十八宿、周天星辰，共一幄。

translations.literal: At the moon altar the principal position was Night Brightness; the Big Dipper, twenty-eight mansions, and all stars under heaven were matched together under one canopy.
translations.idiomatic: At the moon altar Night Brightness held the principal position, with the Big Dipper, twenty-eight mansions, and all stars under heaven matched together under one canopy.

sentences.zh: 天神壇正中，左雲師，次風伯，右雨師，次雷師，南鄉。

translations.literal: Celestial Spirits altar center: left Cloud Master, then Wind Lord; right Rain Master, then Thunder Master—facing south.
translations.idiomatic: At the Celestial Spirits altar the center faced south, with Cloud Master to the left, then Wind Lord, and Rain Master to the right, then Thunder Master.

sentences.zh: 地祇壇正中五嶽，右五鎮，次四海，左五陵，次四瀆，北鄉。

translations.literal: Terrestrial Spirits altar center, the Five Peaks; right, Five Garrisons, then four seas; left, five mausoleum hills, then four rivers—facing north.
translations.idiomatic: At the Terrestrial Spirits altar the Five Peaks held the center, facing north; to the right were the Five Garrisons, then the four seas; to the left five mausoleum hills, then the four rivers.

sentences.zh: 右旁京師山川，左旁天下山川。

translations.literal: To the right, mountains and rivers of the capital; to the left, mountains and rivers of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: To the right stood mountains and rivers of the capital; to the left, mountains and rivers throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 無幄。

translations.literal: No canopies.
translations.idiomatic: There were no canopies.

sentences.zh: 各省府、州、縣神祇位次，正中雲、雨、風、雷，左山川，右城隍。

translations.literal: Spirit position order in each province, prefecture, and county: center, cloud, rain, wind, and thunder; left, mountains and rivers; right, city god.
translations.idiomatic: In each province, prefecture, and county the spirit positions were ordered with cloud, rain, wind, and thunder at the center, mountains and rivers to the left, and the city god to the right.

sentences.zh: 其郊壇神位，皇穹宇、皇乾殿、皇祇室奉之。

translations.literal: Suburban altar spirit tablets were housed in the Imperial Vault of Heaven, Hall of Imperial Heaven, and Chamber of Imperial Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets for the suburban altars were kept in the Imperial Vault of Heaven, Hall of Imperial Heaven, and Chamber of Imperial Earth.

sentences.zh: 神祇、社稷、日月神位，神庫奉之，祭時並移壇所。

translations.literal: Spirit, soil-and-grain, and sun-and-moon tablets were housed in the spirit storehouse and all moved to the altar at sacrifice time.
translations.idiomatic: Tablets for spirits, soil and grain, and sun and moon were kept in the spirit storehouse and moved to the altars when sacrifices were performed.

sentences.zh: 太廟、奉先殿神牌置寢室龕位，祭時移前殿寶座。

translations.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple and Hall of Ancestors spirit tablets were placed in sleeping-chamber niches and moved to the front hall throne at sacrifice time.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Hall of Ancestors rested in sleeping-chamber niches and were moved to the front-hall throne when sacrifices were performed.

sentences.zh: 至傳心殿、歷代帝王、先師各廟龕位，或分或合，無恆制。

translations.literal: As for the Heart-Transmission Hall, successive emperors, and Former Teacher temples, niches were divided or combined with no fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: For the Heart-Transmission Hall, successive emperors, and Former Teacher temples, niches were divided or combined with no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 祭器，圜丘正位，爵三，登一，簠、簋二、籩、豆十，篚、俎、尊各一，配從同。

translations.literal: Sacrificial vessels—Circular Mound principal position: three cups, one platter, two fu and gui, ten biān and dou, one each standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel; matching and attendant the same.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial vessels: at the Circular Mound's principal position were three cups, one platter, two fu and gui, ten biān and dou, and one each standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel; matching and attendant positions were the same.

sentences.zh: 惟大明、夜明■D9三十，夜明鉶皆二，雲、雨、風、雷視夜明。

translations.literal: Only Great Brightness and Night Brightness had thirty standing baskets; Night Brightness meat dishes were two each; cloud, rain, wind, and thunder followed Night Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Only Great Brightness and Night Brightness had thirty standing baskets; Night Brightness had two meat dishes each; cloud, rain, wind, and thunder followed Night Brightness.

sentences.zh: 常雩如冬至、大祀、大雩，正、從位俱籩六、豆二，告祭正位同。

translations.literal: Regular rain prayer like winter solstice, great sacrifice, and great rain prayer—principal and attendant all six biān and two dou; notification sacrifice principal the same.
translations.idiomatic: For the regular rain prayer, as for the winter solstice, great sacrifice, and great rain prayer, principal and attendant positions each had six biān and two dou; notification sacrifices at the principal position followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 方澤祈穀壇正、配位，暨方澤從位，並視圜丘。

translations.literal: Square Mound and Prayer for Grain principal and matching positions, and Square Mound attendant positions, all followed the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Principal and matching positions at the Square Mound and Prayer for Grain altar, and attendant positions at the Square Mound, all followed the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: ■D9、鉶視夜明。

translations.literal: Standing baskets and meat dishes followed Night Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Standing baskets and meat dishes followed Night Brightness.

sentences.zh: 太廟時享，帝、後同案，俱爵三，簠、簋二，籩、豆十有二，登、鉶、篚、俎各一。

translations.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple seasonal offering—emperor and empress on the same table, each three cups, two fu and gui, twelve biān and dou, one each platter, meat dish, standing basket, and chopping block.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple's seasonal offering, emperor and empress shared one table with three cups each, two fu and gui, twelve biān and dou, and one each platter, meat dish, standing basket, and chopping block.

sentences.zh: 尊前後殿同。

translations.literal: Wine vessels in the front and rear halls were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Wine vessels in the front and rear halls were the same.

sentences.zh: 祫祭如時享，東廡每案爵三，簠、簋二，籩、豆十，鉶、篚、俎各一，尊共八案，分二座，爵、鉶倍之。

translations.literal: Joint offering like seasonal offering—east corridor each table three cups, two fu and gui, ten biān and dou, one each meat dish, standing basket, and chopping block; wine vessels eight tables in all, divided into two seats; cups and meat dishes doubled.
translations.idiomatic: The joint offering followed the seasonal offering: each table in the east corridor had three cups, two fu and gui, ten biān and dou, and one each meat dish, standing basket, and chopping block; wine vessels totaled eight tables in two seats, with cups and meat dishes doubled.

sentences.zh: 西廡同，惟簠、簋一，籩、豆四。

translations.literal: West corridor the same, only one fu and gui, four biān and dou.
translations.idiomatic: The west corridor was the same, except for one fu and gui and four biān and dou.

sentences.zh: 告祭，中、後殿俱籩六，豆二。

translations.literal: Notification sacrifice—central and rear halls each six biān and two dou.
translations.idiomatic: For notification sacrifices, the central and rear halls each had six biān and two dou.

sentences.zh: 社稷壇大社、大稷，俱玉爵一，陶爵二，登、篚、俎、尊各一，鉶、簠、簋各二。

translations.literal: Soil and grain altar Great Soil and Great Grain—each one jade cup, two pottery cups, one each platter, standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel; two each meat dish, fu, and gui.
translations.idiomatic: At the altars of soil and grain, Great Soil and Great Grain each had one jade cup and two pottery cups, one each platter, standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel, and two each meat dish, fu, and gui.

sentences.zh: 配位同，惟爵皆用陶。

translations.literal: Matching positions the same, only all cups were pottery.
translations.idiomatic: Matching positions were the same, except that all cups were pottery.

sentences.zh: 祈告，籩六，豆二。

translations.literal: Prayer notification—six biān and two dou.
translations.idiomatic: For prayer notifications there were six biān and two dou.

sentences.zh: 直省祭社稷，爵六，鉶一，籩、豆四，簠、簋、篚、俎、尊各一，如大社稷。

translations.literal: Direct provinces sacrificing at soil and grain—six cups, one meat dish, four biān and dou, one each fu, gui, standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel, as at the great soil and grain altars.
translations.idiomatic: When direct provinces sacrificed at soil and grain, they used six cups, one meat dish, four biān and dou, and one each fu, gui, standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel, as at the great altars.

sentences.zh: 日壇、月壇、先農、先蠶壇，俱爵三，■D9三十，籩、豆十，鉶、簠、簋各二，登、篚、俎、尊各一。

translations.literal: Sun, moon, Former Farmer, and Former Silkworm altars—all three cups, thirty standing baskets, ten biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, one each platter, standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The sun, moon, Former Farmer, and Former Silkworm altars each had three cups, thirty standing baskets, ten biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, and one each platter, standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 直省祭先農如祭社稷。

translations.literal: Direct provinces sacrificing to the Former Farmer followed sacrificing to soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When direct provinces sacrificed to the Former Farmer, they followed the rites for soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 天神壇四案，凡祈祀爵共十二，各用籩六、豆二、尊一、篚一。

translations.literal: Celestial Spirits altar four tables; for prayer sacrifices twelve cups in all, each with six biān, two dou, one wine vessel, and one standing basket.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Spirits altar had four tables; for prayer sacrifices there were twelve cups in all, each table with six biān, two dou, one wine vessel, and one standing basket.

sentences.zh: 地祇壇如之，惟案七共爵二十七耳。

translations.literal: Terrestrial Spirits altar likewise, only seven tables totaling twenty-seven cups.
translations.idiomatic: The Terrestrial Spirits altar was the same, except for seven tables totaling twenty-seven cups.

sentences.zh: 報祀神祇，每案與日壇同，惟無■D9。

translations.literal: Responsive sacrifice to spirits—each table as at the sun altar, only without standing baskets.
translations.idiomatic: For responsive sacrifices to spirits, each table matched the sun altar except that there were no standing baskets.

sentences.zh: 直省祭神祇，爵三，籩、豆四，鉶、簠、簋各二，篚、俎、尊各一。

translations.literal: Direct provinces sacrificing to spirits—three cups, four biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, one each standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: When direct provinces sacrificed to spirits, they used three cups, four biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, and one each standing basket, chopping block, and wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 時巡祭岳鎮、海瀆同。

translations.literal: Tour inspection sacrifice to peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers—the same.
translations.idiomatic: Tour sacrifices to the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 報祀增鉶一，因事遣祭仍用二。

translations.literal: Responsive sacrifice added one meat dish; mission sacrifices dispatched for special affairs still used two.
translations.idiomatic: For responsive sacrifices one meat dish was added; sacrifices dispatched on special occasions still used two.

sentences.zh: 餘同。

translations.literal: The remainder the same.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else was the same.

sentences.zh: 有司致祭無登、■D9。

translations.literal: When officials performed the sacrifice, no platter or bian.
translations.idiomatic: When officials performed the sacrifice, there were no platters or bian.

sentences.zh: 太歲殿准先農，報祀亦如之。

translations.literal: Grand Year Hall followed Former Farmer; responsive sacrifice likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Year Hall followed the Former Farmer altar, and responsive sacrifices did likewise.

sentences.zh: 祈祀，籩六、豆二，不羞俎。

translations.literal: Prayer sacrifice—six biān and two dou, no chopping block offered.
translations.idiomatic: For prayer sacrifices there were six biān and two dou, and no chopping block was set out.

sentences.zh: 先師正位視圜丘，惟用鉶二。

translations.literal: Former Teacher principal position followed Circular Mound, only two meat dishes used.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Teacher's principal position followed the Circular Mound, using only two meat dishes.

sentences.zh: 四配視正位，惟用籩、豆八，無登。

translations.literal: Four correlates followed principal position, only eight biān and dou, no platter.
translations.idiomatic: The four correlates followed the principal position, with only eight biān and dou and no platter.

sentences.zh: 十二哲位，各爵三，鉶一，簠、簋一，籩、豆四，篚、俎、尊共用二。

translations.literal: Twelve philosopher positions—each three cups, one meat dish, one fu and gui, four biān and dou, two shared bian, chopping blocks, and wine vessels.
translations.idiomatic: At the twelve philosophers' positions each had three cups, one meat dish, one fu and gui, four biān and dou, and two each shared bian, chopping blocks, and wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 兩廡二位同案，位一爵，凡獻爵六，共篚二，尊、俎俱各六，簠、簋各一，籩、豆各四。

translations.literal: East and west corridors two positions per table, one cup per position, six cups offered in all, two shared bian, six each wine vessels and chopping blocks, one each fu and gui, four each biān and dou.
translations.idiomatic: In the east and west corridors two positions shared one table with one cup each; six cups were offered in all, with two shared bian, six wine vessels and chopping blocks each, one fu and gui each, and four biān and dou each.

sentences.zh: 視學、釋奠同。

translations.literal: Imperial school inspection and libation ceremony the same.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial school inspections and libation ceremonies followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十三年，頒內府周鼎、尊、卣、罍、壺、簠、簋、觚、爵各一，陳列大成殿，用備禮器。

translations.literal: Qianlong year 33, issued from the inner palace one each Zhou tripod, wine vessel, you, lei, hu, fu, gui, gu, and jue, displayed in the Hall of Great Accomplishment to supply ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 33 the inner palace issued one each of Zhou tripods, wine vessels, you, lei, hu, fu, gui, gu, and jue for display in the Hall of Great Accomplishment as ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 崇聖祠正位五案，案設爵三，籩、豆八，鉶、簠、簋各二，篚、俎、尊各一。

translations.literal: Sage-Veneration Shrine principal five tables—each table three cups, eight biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, one each bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: At the Sage-Veneration Shrine's principal position were five tables, each with three cups, eight biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, and one each bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 配位五案，設爵三，籩、豆四，鉶、篚、簠、簋各一，共俎二，尊二。

translations.literal: Matching five tables—three cups, four biān and dou, one each meat dish, bian, fu, and gui, two chopping blocks and wine vessels shared.
translations.idiomatic: At five matching tables were three cups, four biān and dou, one each meat dish, bian, fu, and gui, and two shared chopping blocks and wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 兩廡三案，案各與配位同，惟共篚為二。

translations.literal: East and west corridors three tables—each as matching positions, only shared bian totaled two.
translations.idiomatic: The east and west corridors had three tables each matching the correlates' layout, except that shared bian totaled two.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十二年，增先師正位籩、豆為十二，崇聖祠籩、豆為十，闕里、直省文廟暨崇聖祠祭器視太學。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 32, increased Former Teacher principal biān and dou to twelve, Sage-Veneration Shrine biān and dou to ten; Qufu, provincial Confucian temples and Sage-Veneration Shrine vessels followed the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 the Former Teacher's principal position was raised to twelve biān and dou and the Sage-Veneration Shrine to ten; temples at Qufu, in the direct provinces, and at the Sage-Veneration Shrine followed the Imperial Academy for sacrificial vessels.

sentences.zh: 歷代帝王正位十六案，案設爵三，登一，鉶、簠、簋各二，籩、豆十，篚一，共俎七，尊七。

translations.literal: Successive emperors principal sixteen tables—each table three cups, one platter, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, ten biān and dou, one bian, seven chopping blocks and wine vessels shared.
translations.idiomatic: At the successive emperors' principal position were sixteen tables, each with three cups, one platter, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, ten biān and dou, one bian, and seven shared chopping blocks and wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 兩廡配位二十案，案設爵十二，鉶二，籩、豆四，簠、簋、篚各一，共俎四，尊四。

translations.literal: East and west corridor matching twenty tables—each table twelve cups, two meat dishes, four biān and dou, one each fu, gui, and bian, four chopping blocks and wine vessels shared.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty matching tables in the east and west corridors each had twelve cups, two meat dishes, four biān and dou, one each fu, gui, and bian, and four shared chopping blocks and wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 傳心殿正位九案，案設爵、尊各三，鉶、篚各一，籩、豆二。

translations.literal: Heart-Transmission Hall principal nine tables—each table three cups and wine vessels, one each meat dish and bian, two biān and dou.
translations.idiomatic: At the Heart-Transmission Hall's principal position were nine tables, each with three cups and wine vessels, one each meat dish and bian, and two biān and dou.

sentences.zh: 配位二案，案設爵三，籩、豆二，鉶、篚、尊各一。

translations.literal: Matching two tables—each table three cups, two biān and dou, one each meat dish, bian, and wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Two matching tables each had three cups, two biān and dou, and one each meat dish, bian, and wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 關帝、文昌帝君俱爵三，籩、豆十，鉶、簠、簋各二，登、篚、俎、尊各一，惟後殿籩、豆八。

translations.literal: Lord Guan and Lord of Literary Glory each three cups, ten biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, one each platter, bian, chopping block, and wine vessel—only rear hall eight biān and dou.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Guan and the Lord of Literary Glory each had three cups, ten biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, and one each platter, bian, chopping block, and wine vessel; only the rear halls had eight biān and dou.

sentences.zh: 各省准京式。

translations.literal: Each province followed the capital pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Every province followed the capital pattern.

sentences.zh: 先醫三皇位，位設爵三，籩、豆十，簠、簋、篚、俎、尊各一。

translations.literal: Former Physician three emperor positions—each position three cups, ten biān and dou, one each fu, gui, bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: At the Former Physician's three emperor positions each had three cups, ten biān and dou, and one each fu, gui, bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 兩廡六案，案設簋、簠一，篚、尊各二，籩、豆四，共爵六。

translations.literal: East and west corridors six tables—each table one gui and fu, two each bian and wine vessel, four biān and dou, six cups shared.
translations.idiomatic: The east and west corridors had six tables, each with one gui and fu, two each bian and wine vessel, four biān and dou, and six cups shared.

sentences.zh: 都城隍爵三，籩、豆十，鉶、簠、簋各二，篚、俎、尊各一。

translations.literal: Capital city god three cups, ten biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, one each bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The capital city god had three cups, ten biān and dou, two each meat dish, fu, and gui, and one each bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 火神、東嶽廟，俱果盤五，篚、俎、尊各一。

translations.literal: Fire Spirit and Eastern Peak temples—each five fruit trays, one each bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The Fire Spirit and Eastern Peak temples each had five fruit trays and one each bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 黑龍潭、玉泉山、昆明湖各龍神祠、惠濟祠、河神廟俱三案，案設爵三，簠、簋二，籩、豆十，篚、俎、尊各一。

translations.literal: Black Dragon Pool, Jade Spring Mountain, Kunming Lake dragon spirit shrines, Beneficent Aid Shrine, and River God Temple—each three tables; each table three cups, two fu and gui, ten biān and dou, one each bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon spirit shrines at Black Dragon Pool, Jade Spring Mountain, and Kunming Lake, the Beneficent Aid Shrine, and the River God Temple each had three tables with three cups, two fu and gui, ten biān and dou, and one each bian, chopping block, and wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 初沿明舊，壇廟祭品遵古制，惟器用瓷。

translations.literal: Initially they followed Ming usage; altar and temple offerings observed antiquity, only vessels used porcelain.
translations.idiomatic: At first the dynasty followed Ming practice: altar and temple offerings observed ancient regulations, but vessels were porcelain.

sentences.zh: 雍正時，改范銅。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period they were changed to cast copper.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng they were changed to cast copper.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，詔祭品宜法古，命廷臣集議，始定制籩編竹，絲絹里，魨漆。

translations.literal: Qianlong year 13, edict that sacrificial offerings should follow antiquity; court ministers were ordered to deliberate, and regulations were first fixed—biān woven of bamboo, lined with silk, coated with t'o lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 an edict held that sacrificial offerings should follow antiquity; the emperor ordered court ministers to deliberate, and regulations were first fixed: biān woven of bamboo, lined with silk, and coated with t'o lacquer.

sentences.zh: 郊壇純漆，太廟采畫。

translations.literal: Suburban altars plain lacquer; Imperial Ancestral Temple painted.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban altars used plain lacquer; the Imperial Ancestral Temple used painted decoration.

sentences.zh: 其豆、登、簠、簋，郊壇用陶，太廟惟登用之，其他用木，魨漆，飾金玉。

translations.literal: Dou, platter, fu, and gui—suburban altars used pottery; Imperial Ancestral Temple only the platter was pottery, the rest wood with t'o lacquer, adorned with gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: For dou, platters, fu, and gui, suburban altars used pottery; at the Imperial Ancestral Temple only the platter was pottery, while the rest were wood with t'o lacquer and adorned with gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 鉶范銅飾金。

translations.literal: Meat dishes cast copper adorned with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Meat dishes were cast in copper and adorned with gold.

sentences.zh: 尊則郊壇用陶。

translations.literal: Wine vessels—suburban altars used pottery.
translations.idiomatic: Wine vessels at suburban altars were pottery.

sentences.zh: 太廟春犧尊、夏象尊、秋著尊、冬壺尊、祫祭山尊，均范銅。

translations.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple spring sacrificial vessel, summer elephant vessel, autumn zhu vessel, winter pot vessel, and joint-offering mountain vessel—all cast copper.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple the spring sacrificial vessel, summer elephant vessel, autumn zhu vessel, winter pot vessel, and joint-offering mountain vessel were all cast in copper.

sentences.zh: 祀天地爵用匏，太廟玉，兩廡陶。

translations.literal: Sacrificing Heaven and Earth cups used gourd; Imperial Ancestral Temple jade; east and west corridors pottery.
translations.idiomatic: Cups for sacrificing Heaven and Earth were gourd; at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, jade; in the east and west corridors, pottery.

sentences.zh: 社稷正位，玉一陶二。

translations.literal: Soil and grain principal position—one jade, two pottery.
translations.idiomatic: At the soil and grain principal position were one jade cup and two pottery cups.

sentences.zh: 配位純陶。

translations.literal: Matching positions pure pottery.
translations.idiomatic: Matching positions used pottery only.

sentences.zh: 又豆、登、簠、簋、鉶、尊皆陶。

translations.literal: Again dou, platter, fu, gui, meat dish, and wine vessel all pottery.
translations.idiomatic: Again, dou, platters, fu, gui, meat dishes, and wine vessels were all pottery.

sentences.zh: 日、月、先農、先蠶亦如之。

translations.literal: Sun, moon, Former Farmer, and Former Silkworm likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The sun, moon, Former Farmer, and Former Silkworm altars were the same.

sentences.zh: 帝王、先師、關帝、文昌及諸祠，則皆用銅。

translations.literal: Successive emperors, Former Teacher, Lord Guan, Lord of Literary Glory, and various shrines—all used copper.
translations.idiomatic: For successive emperors, the Former Teacher, Lord Guan, the Lord of Literary Glory, and various shrines, all used copper.

sentences.zh: 凡陶必辨色，圜丘、祈穀、常雩青，方澤、社稷、先農黃，日壇赤，月壇白。

translations.literal: All pottery must distinguish color—Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, and regular rain prayer green; Square Mound, soil and grain, and Former Farmer yellow; sun altar red; moon altar white.
translations.idiomatic: All pottery had to be color-coded: the Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, and regular rain prayer used green; the Square Mound, soil and grain, and Former Farmer yellow; the sun altar red; the moon altar white.

sentences.zh: 太廟陶登，黃質采飾，餘俱白。

translations.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple pottery platter yellow body with painted decoration; the rest all white.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ancestral Temple's pottery platter had a yellow body with painted decoration; all others were white.

sentences.zh: 盛帛用竹篚，魨色如其器。

translations.literal: Silk was held in bamboo bian; t'o lacquer color matched its vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Silk was held in bamboo bian, with t'o lacquer colored to match the vessel.

sentences.zh: 載牲用木俎，魨以丹漆。

translations.literal: Victims were borne on wooden chopping blocks coated with red t'o lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Victims were borne on wooden chopping blocks coated with red t'o lacquer.

sentences.zh: 毛血盤用陶，色亦如其器。

translations.literal: Fur-and-blood trays were pottery, color also matching their vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Fur-and-blood trays were pottery, their color also matching the vessel.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，定太廟簠、簋、豆與凡祭祀竹籩，三歲一修。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 19, fixed Imperial Ancestral Temple fu, gui, dou, and bamboo biān for all sacrifices—repaired every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 it was fixed that Imperial Ancestral Temple fu, gui, dou, and bamboo biān for all sacrifices were to be repaired every three years.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十二年，先師爵改用玉。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 32, Former Teacher cups changed to jade.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 the Former Teacher's cups were changed to jade.

sentences.zh: 祭品，凡籩、豆之實各十二，籩用形鹽、薨魚、棗、栗、榛、菱、芡、鹿脯、白餅、黑餅、糗餌、粉餈，豆用韭菹、醓醢、菁菹、鹿醢、芹菹、兔醢、筍菹、魚醢、脾析、豚拍、酏食、糝食。

translations.literal: Sacrificial offerings—fillings for biān and dou each twelve: biān used molded salt, dried fish, dates, chestnuts, hazelnuts, water caltrop, gorgon fruit, dried venison, white cake, black cake, parched-grain cakes, and powdered cakes; dou used leek pickle, fermented sauce and minced meat, smartweed pickle, venison paste, celery pickle, hare paste, bamboo-shoot pickle, fish paste, spleen and tripe, pork shoulder, fermented drink, and grain garnish.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrificial offerings, biān and dou each held twelve items: biān held molded salt, dried fish, dates, chestnuts, hazelnuts, water caltrop, gorgon fruit, dried venison, white cake, black cake, parched-grain cakes, and powdered cakes; dou held leek pickle, fermented sauce and minced meat, smartweed pickle, venison paste, celery pickle, hare paste, bamboo-shoot pickle, fish paste, spleen and tripe, pork shoulder, fermented drink, and grain garnish.

sentences.zh: 用十者，籩減糗餌、粉餈，豆減酏食、糝食。

translations.literal: Where ten were used—biān omitted parched-grain and powdered cakes; dou omitted fermented drink and grain garnish.
translations.idiomatic: Where ten were used, biān omitted parched-grain and powdered cakes and dou omitted fermented drink and grain garnish.

sentences.zh: 用八者，籩減白、黑餅，豆減脾析、豚拍。

translations.literal: Where eight were used—biān omitted white and black cakes; dou omitted spleen and tripe and pork shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Where eight were used, biān omitted white and black cakes and dou omitted spleen and tripe and pork shoulder.

sentences.zh: 用四者，籩止實形鹽、棗、栗、鹿脯，豆止實菁菹、鹿醢、芹菹、兔醢。

translations.literal: Where four were used—biān held only molded salt, dates, chestnuts, and dried venison; dou held only smartweed pickle, venison paste, celery pickle, and hare paste.
translations.idiomatic: Where four were used, biān held only molded salt, dates, chestnuts, and dried venison, and dou only smartweed pickle, venison paste, celery pickle, and hare paste.

sentences.zh: 籩六者，用鹿脯、棗、榛、葡萄、桃仁、蓮實。

translations.literal: Six biān used dried venison, dates, hazelnuts, grapes, peach kernels, and lotus seeds.
translations.idiomatic: Six biān used dried venison, dates, hazelnuts, grapes, peach kernels, and lotus seeds.

sentences.zh: 豆二者，止用鹿醢、兔醢。

translations.literal: Two dou used only venison paste and hare paste.
translations.idiomatic: Two dou used only venison paste and hare paste.

sentences.zh: 登一，太羹。

translations.literal: One platter—supreme broth.
translations.idiomatic: One platter held supreme broth.

sentences.zh: 鉶二，和羹。

translations.literal: Two meat dishes—harmonized broth.
translations.idiomatic: Two meat dishes held harmonized broth.

sentences.zh: 簠二，稻、粱。

translations.literal: Two fu—rice and millet.
translations.idiomatic: Two fu held rice and millet.

sentences.zh: 簋二，黍、稷。

translations.literal: Two gui—panicled millet and glutinous millet.
translations.idiomatic: Two gui held panicled millet and glutinous millet.

sentences.zh: 玉、帛、牲牢：玉六等，上帝蒼璧，皇地祇黃琮，大社黃珪，大稷青珪，朝日赤璧，夕月白璧。

translations.literal: Jade, silk, and victim herds—jade six grades: Supreme God green disc, Imperial Earth yellow tube, Great Soil yellow tablet, Great Grain green tablet, Morning Sun red disc, Evening Moon white disc.
translations.idiomatic: Jade, silk, and victim herds: jade had six grades—the Supreme God a green disc, Imperial Earth a yellow tube, Great Soil a yellow tablet, Great Grain a green tablet, Morning Sun a red disc, and Evening Moon a white disc.

sentences.zh: 舊制，社稷壇春秋常祀用玉，禱祀則否。

translations.literal: Former regulations: soil-and-grain altar spring and autumn regular sacrifices used jade; prayer sacrifices did not.
translations.idiomatic: Under former regulations the soil-and-grain altar used jade for spring and autumn regular sacrifices but not for prayer sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十四年，會天旱禱雨，諭曰：「玉以芘廕嘉穀，俾免水旱偏災，特敕所司用玉將事。

translations.literal: Qianlong year 34, when drought led to rain prayer, edict said: "Jade is to shelter and bless the fine grain, that partial disasters of flood and drought may be avoided; I specially order the responsible offices to use jade in performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 34, when drought occasioned rain prayer, the emperor's edict read: "Jade is to shelter and bless the fine grain, that partial disasters of flood and drought may be avoided; I specially order the responsible offices to use jade in performing the rite.

sentences.zh: 」自此為恆式。

translations.literal: " From this it became constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: From this it became the constant practice.

sentences.zh: 帛七等：曰郊祀制帛，南北郊用之。

translations.literal: Silk seven grades: called suburban-sacrifice regulated silk, used at the southern and northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Silk had seven grades: suburban-sacrifice regulated silk, used at the southern and northern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 上帝青十二，地祇黃一。

translations.literal: Supreme God green twelve, Imperial Earth yellow one.
translations.idiomatic: For the Supreme God, twelve green; for Imperial Earth, one yellow.

sentences.zh: 曰禮神制帛，社稷以下用之。

translations.literal: Called spirit-rite regulated silk, used from soil and grain downward.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-rite regulated silk was used from soil and grain downward.

sentences.zh: 社稷黑四，大明赤一，夜明白一，日月同。

translations.literal: Soil and grain black four, Great Brightness red one, Night Brightness white one—sun and moon the same.
translations.idiomatic: Soil and grain had four black; Great Brightness one red; Night Brightness one white; sun and moon the same.

sentences.zh: 星辰斗宿白七，青、赤、黃、黑各一。

translations.literal: Stars and Dipper mansions white seven, green, red, yellow, and black one each.
translations.idiomatic: Stars and Dipper mansions had seven white, and one each green, red, yellow, and black.

sentences.zh: 天神、雲、雨、風、雷，青、白、黃、黑各一，方澤從位，岳鎮各五，五色。

translations.literal: Celestial spirits, cloud, rain, wind, and thunder—green, white, yellow, and black one each; Square Mound attendant positions peaks and garrisons five each, five colors.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial spirits, cloud, rain, wind, and thunder had one each green, white, yellow, and black; Square Mound attendant positions had five each for peaks and garrisons in five colors.

sentences.zh: 五陵山白五。

translations.literal: Five mausoleum hills white five.
translations.idiomatic: Five mausoleum hills had five white.

sentences.zh: 四海隨方為色。

translations.literal: Four seas followed direction for color.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas followed their direction for color.

sentences.zh: 四瀆黑四。

translations.literal: Four rivers black four.
translations.idiomatic: Four rivers had four black.

sentences.zh: 地祇黃二，青、赤各三，黑七、白十二。

translations.literal: Imperial Earth yellow two, green and red three each, black seven and white twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Earth had two yellow, three each green and red, seven black, and twelve white.

sentences.zh: 先農、先蠶俱青一，先師正、配位，十二哲，兩廡，崇聖祠正位，東、西廡，俱各一用白。

translations.literal: Former Farmer and Former Silkworm each green one; Former Teacher principal and correlates, twelve philosophers, east and west corridors, Sage-Veneration Shrine principal, east and west corridors—all one white each.
translations.idiomatic: Former Farmer and Former Silkworm each had one green; Former Teacher principal and correlates, twelve philosophers, east and west corridors, and Sage-Veneration Shrine principal and east and west corridors each had one white.

sentences.zh: 帝王各位、關帝、文昌正位、後殿，太歲正位，北極佑聖真君、東嶽都城隍亦如之。

translations.literal: Successive emperors each position, Lord Guan, Lord of Literary Glory principal and rear hall, Grand Year principal, North Pole Protecting Sage True Lord, and Eastern Peak capital city god likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Successive emperors at each position, Lord Guan, the Lord of Literary Glory at principal and rear halls, Grand Year principal position, North Pole Protecting Sage True Lord, and Eastern Peak capital city god were the same.

sentences.zh: 惟先醫正位三，崇聖配位四，太歲兩廡十二，火神赤一。

translations.literal: Only Former Physician principal three, Sage-Veneration correlates four, Grand Year east and west corridors twelve, Fire Spirit one red.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Former Physician principal had three, Sage-Veneration correlates four, Grand Year east and west corridors twelve, and Fire Spirit one red.

sentences.zh: 曰告祀制幣，祈報祭告用之。

translations.literal: Called prayer-and-response regulated silk, used for prayer and responsive notification sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer-and-response regulated silk was used for prayer and responsive notification sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 祈穀、雩祀、告祀圜丘俱青一，祭告方澤黃一。

translations.literal: Prayer for Grain, rain prayer, and notification sacrifice at Circular Mound each green one; notification sacrifice at Square Mound yellow one.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer for Grain, rain prayer, and notification sacrifice at the Circular Mound each had one green; notification sacrifice at the Square Mound one yellow.

sentences.zh: 曰奉先制幣，郊祀配位、太廟用之，圜丘、方澤配位各一，太廟帝後每位一。

translations.literal: Called honoring-ancestors regulated silk, used for suburban correlate positions and Imperial Ancestral Temple—Circular Mound and Square Mound correlates one each, Imperial Ancestral Temple each emperor and empress one.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring-ancestors regulated silk was used for suburban correlate positions and the Imperial Ancestral Temple: Circular Mound and Square Mound correlates one each, and at the Imperial Ancestral Temple one for each emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 曰展親制幣，親王配饗用之，太廟東廡位各一。

translations.literal: Called extending-kinship regulated silk, used when princes were matched in feasting—Imperial Ancestral Temple east corridor one each.
translations.idiomatic: Extending-kinship regulated silk was used when princes were matched in feasting: one each at Imperial Ancestral Temple east corridor positions.

sentences.zh: 曰報功制幣，功臣配饗用之，太廟西廡位各一。

translations.literal: Called reporting-merit regulated silk, used when meritorious ministers were matched in feasting—Imperial Ancestral Temple west corridor one each.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting-merit regulated silk was used when meritorious ministers were matched in feasting: one each at Imperial Ancestral Temple west corridor positions.

sentences.zh: 三者俱白，昭忠等祠同，並織滿、漢文字。

translations.literal: All three white; Loyalty and Fidelity shrines the same, all woven with Manchu and Chinese characters.
translations.idiomatic: All three were white; Loyalty and Fidelity shrines were the same, all woven with Manchu and Chinese characters.

sentences.zh: 曰素帛，帝王廟兩廡位各一，先醫廟兩廡共四，餘祀亦尚素。

translations.literal: Called plain silk—successive emperors' temple east and west corridors one each, Former Physician temple east and west corridors four shared, remaining sacrifices also favored plain.
translations.idiomatic: Plain silk: successive emperors' temple east and west corridors one each, Former Physician temple east and west corridors four shared; remaining sacrifices also favored plain.

sentences.zh: 牲牢四等：曰犢，曰特，曰太牢，曰少牢。

translations.literal: Victim herds four grades: called calf, called special victim, called great herd, called lesser herd.
translations.idiomatic: Victim herds had four grades: calf, special victim, great herd, and lesser herd.

sentences.zh: 色尚騂或黝。

translations.literal: Color favored sorrel or dark.
translations.idiomatic: Color favored sorrel or dark-coated animals.

sentences.zh: 圜丘、方澤用犢，大明、夜明用特，天神、地祇、太歲、日、月、星辰、雲、雨、風、雷、社稷、岳鎮、海瀆、太廟、先農、先蠶、先師、帝王、關帝、文昌用太牢。

translations.literal: Circular Mound and Square Mound used calf; Great Brightness and Night Brightness used special victim; celestial spirits, terrestrial spirits, Grand Year, sun, moon, stars, cloud, rain, wind, thunder, soil and grain, peaks and garrisons, seas and rivers, Imperial Ancestral Temple, Former Farmer, Former Silkworm, Former Teacher, successive emperors, Lord Guan, and Lord of Literary Glory used great herd.
translations.idiomatic: The Circular Mound and Square Mound used a calf; Great Brightness and Night Brightness a special victim; celestial spirits, terrestrial spirits, Grand Year, sun, moon, stars, cloud, rain, wind, thunder, soil and grain, peaks and garrisons, seas and rivers, Imperial Ancestral Temple, Former Farmer, Former Silkworm, Former Teacher, successive emperors, Lord Guan, and the Lord of Literary Glory used the great herd.

sentences.zh: 太廟西廡，文廟配哲、崇聖祠、帝王廟兩廡，關帝、文昌後殿，用少牢。

translations.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple west corridor, Confucian temple correlate philosophers, Sage-Veneration Shrine, successive emperors' temple east and west corridors, Lord Guan and Lord of Literary Glory rear halls used lesser herd.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ancestral Temple west corridor, Confucian temple correlate philosophers, Sage-Veneration Shrine, successive emperors' temple east and west corridors, and Lord Guan and Lord of Literary Glory rear halls used the lesser herd.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十二年，崇聖正位改太牢。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 32, Sage-Veneration principal changed to great herd.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 the Sage-Veneration principal position was changed to the great herd.

sentences.zh: 直省神祇、社稷、先農、關帝、先醫配位暨群祀用少牢。

translations.literal: Direct-province spirits, soil and grain, Former Farmer, Lord Guan, Former Physician correlates, and mass sacrifices used lesser herd.
translations.idiomatic: Direct-province spirits, soil and grain, Former Farmer, Lord Guan, Former Physician correlates, and mass sacrifices used the lesser herd.

sentences.zh: 火神、東嶽、先醫正位，都城隍，皆太牢。

translations.literal: Fire Spirit, Eastern Peak, Former Physician principal, capital city god—all great herd.
translations.idiomatic: Fire Spirit, Eastern Peak, Former Physician principal, and capital city god all used the great herd.

sentences.zh: 太牢：羊一、牛一、豕一，少牢：羊、豕各一。

translations.literal: Great herd: one sheep, one ox, one pig; lesser herd: one sheep and one pig each.
translations.idiomatic: The great herd comprised one sheep, one ox, and one pig; the lesser herd one sheep and one pig each.

sentences.zh: 大祀入滌九旬，中祀六旬，群祀三旬。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice purging ninety days, middle sacrifice sixty days, mass sacrifice thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifices required ninety days of purging, middle sacrifices sixty, and mass sacrifices thirty.

sentences.zh: 大祀天地，前期五日親王視牲，二日禮部尚書省牲，一日子時宰牲。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice Heaven and Earth—five days before, princes inspected victims; two days before, Minister of Rites inspected victims; at zi hour on the last day victims were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: For the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, five days beforehand princes inspected the victims, two days before the Minister of Rites inspected them, and at the zi hour on the final day the victims were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 帝祭天壇，前二日酉時宰之，太廟、社稷、先師前三日，中祀前二日。

translations.literal: When the emperor sacrificed at the Heaven Altar, slaughter was at you hour two days before; Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain, and Former Teacher three days before; middle sacrifices two days before.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sacrificed at the Heaven Altar, slaughter came at you hour two days before; for the Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain, and Former Teacher, three days before; for middle sacrifices, two days before.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書率太常司省牲，前一日黎明宰牲。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites leading Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials inspected victims; on the preceding day at dawn victims were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites led Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials to inspect victims; on the preceding day at dawn the victims were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 惟夕月屆日黎明宰之。

translations.literal: Only Evening Moon on the day itself at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Only Evening Moon was slaughtered at dawn on the day itself.

sentences.zh: 令甲，察院、禮部、太常、光祿官監宰，群祀止太常司行。

translations.literal: By regulation, Censorate, Ministry of Rites, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Court of Imperial Entertainments officials supervised slaughter; mass sacrifices only the Court of Imperial Sacrifices conducted them.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation the Censorate, Ministry of Rites, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Court of Imperial Entertainments supervised slaughter; for mass sacrifices only the Court of Imperial Sacrifices performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，定大祀、中祀用光祿卿監宰。

translations.literal: Qianlong year 17, fixed great and middle sacrifices to use the Court of Imperial Entertainments director supervising slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 17 it was fixed that great and middle sacrifices used the Court of Imperial Entertainments director to supervise slaughter.

sentences.zh: 初，郊壇大祀，帝前期宿齋宮，視壇位、籩豆、牲牢。

translations.literal: Initially, for suburban altar great sacrifices the emperor beforehand lodged in the fasting palace and inspected altar positions, biān, dou, and victim herds.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, for suburban altar great sacrifices the emperor beforehand lodged in the fasting palace and inspected altar positions, biān, dou, and victim herds.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，更定前一日帝詣圜丘視壇位，分獻官詣神庫視籩豆，神廚視牲牢。

translations.literal: Qianlong year 7, revised so that on the preceding day the emperor went to the Circular Mound to inspect altar positions; presentation officials went to the spirit storehouse to inspect biān and dou, and the spirit kitchen to inspect victim herds.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 7 this was revised: on the preceding day the emperor went to the Circular Mound to inspect altar positions; presentation officials went to the spirit storehouse to inspect biān and dou and the spirit kitchen to inspect victim herds.

sentences.zh: 尋定視壇位日，親詣皇穹宇、皇乾殿上香。

translations.literal: Soon fixed that on the day of inspecting altar positions the emperor in person went to the Imperial Vault of Heaven and Hall of Imperial Heaven to offer incense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was fixed that on the day of inspecting altar positions the emperor in person went to the Imperial Vault of Heaven and Hall of Imperial Heaven to offer incense.

sentences.zh: 故事，省視籩豆牲牢，或臨視，或否。

translations.literal: By precedent, provincial inspection of biān, dou, and victim herds—sometimes inspected in person, sometimes not.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, officials inspected biān, dou, and victim herds in advance; the emperor sometimes inspected in person and sometimes did not.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，定遣官將事，自後以為常。

translations.literal: Year 35, fixed dispatching officials to preside; thereafter made regular.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year it was fixed to dispatch officials to preside over the rites; thereafter this became regular practice.

sentences.zh: 祀期郊廟祭祀，祭前二歲十月，欽天監豫卜吉期。

translations.literal: Sacrifice dates for suburban altar and temple sacrifices: two years before the sacrifice, tenth month, Directorate of Astronomy pre-selected auspicious dates.
translations.idiomatic: For scheduled suburban altar and temple sacrifices, in the tenth month two years before the rite the Directorate of Astronomy pre-selected auspicious dates.

sentences.zh: 前一歲正月，疏卜吉者及諸祀定有日者以聞。

translations.literal: First month of the year before, memorialized those with auspicious dates selected and all sacrifices with fixed days to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the year before, a memorial listed those with auspicious dates chosen and every sacrifice with a fixed day, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 頒示中外。

translations.literal: Promulgated within and without.
translations.idiomatic: This was promulgated throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 太常寺按祀期先期題請，實禮部主之。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices according to sacrifice dates beforehand submitted requests; in fact Ministry of Rites presided.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted requests ahead of time according to the sacrifice calendar; in practice the Ministry of Rites oversaw the matter.

sentences.zh: 世祖纘業，詔祭祀各分等次，以時致祭。

translations.literal: Founding Emperor continuing the enterprise, decreed sacrifices each divided into grades, at seasons offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor succeeded to the enterprise, he decreed that sacrifices be graded and offered at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 自是大祀、中祀、群祀先後規定祀期，著為例。

translations.literal: From this great sacrifice, middle sacrifice, mass sacrifice in sequence regulated sacrifice dates, established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter great, middle, and mass sacrifices had their dates regulated in sequence and established as precedent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年，復定大、中祀遇忌辰不改祀期。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 7, again fixed great and middle sacrifice encountering taboo anniversary not changing sacrifice date.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 7 it was reaffirmed that great and middle sacrifices did not change their dates when they fell on a taboo anniversary.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，更定關帝、文昌春秋祀期不用忌辰。

translations.literal: Within Xianfeng, again fixed Guandi, Wenchang spring and autumn sacrifice dates not using taboo anniversary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign it was revised that the spring and autumn sacrifice dates for Guandi and Wenchang did not follow taboo anniversaries.

sentences.zh: 其祭祀時刻，順治十三年，詔祭天、地五鼓出宮，社稷、太廟並黎明。

translations.literal: Their sacrifice hours: Shunzhi year 13, decreed sacrificing Heaven, Earth at fifth drum leave palace; soil and grain, Imperial Ancestral Temple both at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: As for the hour of sacrifice: in Shunzhi 13 an edict fixed sacrifices to Heaven and Earth so that the procession left the palace at the fifth drum; the soil-and-grain and Imperial Ancestral Temple rites both came at dawn.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，依太宗舊制，壇廟用黎明，夕月用酉時。

translations.literal: Kangxi year 12, following Taizong old system, altars and temples used dawn, Evening Moon used you hour.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12, following Taizong's former system, altar and temple rites used dawn and Evening Moon used the you hour.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶八年，諭祭祀行禮，當在寅卯間，合禮經質明將事古義。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 8, instructed sacrifice performing rites should be between yin and mao, matching Rites classic clear-dawn commence affairs ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 8 the throne instructed that sacrificial rites be performed between the yin and mao hours, in keeping with the ancient meaning of the Rites' 'at clear dawn commence the affair.'

sentences.zh: 凡親行大祀，所司定時刻，承祭官暨執事陪祭者祗候，率意遲早者，御史糾之。

translations.literal: Whenever personally performing great sacrifice, responsible office fixed hour, presiding sacrificer together with ritual and attendant sacrificers reverently waited; those who heedlessly came early or late, censors impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor personally performed a great sacrifice, the responsible office fixed the hour and the presiding sacrificer together with ritual and attendant sacrificers waited in reverence; censors impeached anyone who came early or late at whim.

sentences.zh: 齋戒順治三年，定郊祀齋戒儀。

translations.literal: Fasting purification: Shunzhi year 3, fixed suburban sacrifice fasting purification rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fasting and purification: in Shunzhi 3 the suburban sacrifice fasting rites were fixed.

sentences.zh: 八年，定大祀三日、中祀二日公廨置齋戒木牌。

translations.literal: Year 8, fixed great sacrifice three days, middle sacrifice two days official quarters set fasting wooden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 it was fixed that great sacrifices required three days and middle sacrifices two days, with fasting wooden tablets displayed in official quarters.

sentences.zh: 祀前十日，錄齋戒人名冊致太常，屆日不讞刑獄，不宴會，不聽樂，不宿內，不飲酒、茹葷，不問疾、弔喪，不祭神、掃墓。

translations.literal: Ten days before sacrifice, recorded fasting persons' name register sent to Court of Imperial Sacrifices; on the day no criminal judgments, no banquets, no listening to music, no lodging inside, no drinking wine or eating meat, no inquiring after illness or mourning, no sacrificing to spirits or sweeping tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days before the sacrifice a register of those fasting was sent to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; on the appointed days they passed no criminal judgments, held no banquets, heard no music, lodged nowhere inside the palace, drank no wine and ate no meat, paid no sick-visits or mourning calls, and sacrificed to no spirits or swept no tombs.

sentences.zh: 有疾與服勿與。

translations.literal: Those with illness and mourning do not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were ill or in mourning did not take part.

sentences.zh: 大祀、中祀，太常司進齋戒牌、銅人置乾清門黃案。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice, middle sacrifice, Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented fasting tablets, bronze man placed Gate of Heavenly Purity yellow desk.
translations.idiomatic: For great and middle sacrifices the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented fasting tablets and a bronze figure placed on the yellow desk at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 大祀前三日，帝致齋大內，頒誓戒。

translations.literal: Three days before great sacrifice, emperor fasted inner palace, issued oath of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before a great sacrifice the emperor fasted within the inner palace and issued the oath of admonition.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「惟爾群臣，其蠲乃心、齊乃志，各揚其職。

translations.literal: Text reads: "O you ministers, purify your hearts and align your wills; each perform your charge.
translations.idiomatic: The text read: "O you ministers, purify your hearts and align your wills; each perform your charge.

sentences.zh: 敢或不共，國有常刑。

translations.literal: If any dare be inattentive, the state has standing punishments.
translations.idiomatic: If any dare be remiss, the state has standing punishments.

sentences.zh: 欽哉勿怠！

translations.literal: Reverently—do not be remiss!"
translations.idiomatic: Reverently—do not be remiss!"

sentences.zh: 」前祀一日，徹牌及銅人送齋宮，帝詣壇齋宿。

translations.literal: One day before sacrifice, removed tablets and bronze man and sent to fasting palace; emperor went to altar to fast overnight.
translations.idiomatic: One day before the sacrifice the tablets and bronze figure were removed and sent to the fasting palace, and the emperor went to the altar to fast overnight.

sentences.zh: 十四年祀圜丘，致齋大內二日，壇內齋宮一日。

translations.literal: Year 14 sacrificing at Circular Mound, fasted inner palace two days, within altar fasting palace one day.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, when sacrificing at the Circular Mound, he fasted in the inner palace for two days and in the altar fasting palace for one.

sentences.zh: 陪祭官齋於公署，圜丘齋於壇。

translations.literal: Attendant sacrificers fasted at official quarters; Circular Mound fasted at altar.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant sacrificers fasted at their official quarters; for the Circular Mound they fasted at the altar.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，遣御史等赴壇檢視。

translations.literal: Yongzheng year 5, dispatched censors and others to altar to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 censors and others were dispatched to the altar to inspect preparations.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔科道遇祀期齋戒。

translations.literal: Year 9, decreed censorial and supervising officials observe fasting on sacrifice dates.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 an edict required censorial and supervising officials to keep fasting when sacrifice dates arrived.

sentences.zh: 明年，仿明祀牌制制齋牌，敕陪祭官懸佩，防褻慢。

translations.literal: Next year, imitating Ming sacrifice tablet system made fasting tablets, commanded attendant sacrificers suspend and wear them, guard against irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, imitating the Ming sacrifice-tablet system, fasting tablets were made and attendant sacrificers were commanded to wear them suspended from the belt to guard against irreverence.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年，禮臣奏，郊壇大祀，太常卿先期四日具齋戒期，進牌及銅人置乾清門二日、齋宮一日。

translations.literal: Qianlong year 4, rites ministers memorialized: suburban altar great sacrifice, Court of Imperial Sacrifices director four days beforehand prepared fasting schedule, presented tablets and bronze man placed Gate of Heavenly Purity two days, fasting palace one day.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 4 the ministers of rites memorialized that for suburban altar great sacrifices the Court of Imperial Sacrifices director, four days in advance, should prepare the fasting schedule and present the tablets and bronze figure to be placed at the Gate of Heavenly Purity for two days and at the fasting palace for one.

sentences.zh: 太廟、社稷，置乾清門三日。

translations.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain, placed Gate of Heavenly Purity three days.
translations.idiomatic: For the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the altars of soil and grain they were placed at the Gate of Heavenly Purity for three days.

sentences.zh: 中祀，前三日奏進，置乾清門二日。

translations.literal: Middle sacrifice, three days before memorialized and presented, placed Gate of Heavenly Purity two days.
translations.idiomatic: For middle sacrifices they were memorialized and presented three days beforehand and placed at the Gate of Heavenly Purity for two days.

sentences.zh: 並祭日徹還。

translations.literal: All on sacrifice day removed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice they were all removed and returned.

sentences.zh: 後饗先蠶，奏進亦如之。

translations.literal: Empress sacrificing to Silkworm Goddess, memorialized and presented likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress sacrificed to the Silkworm Goddess, the presentation followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 惟由內侍置交泰殿三日。

translations.literal: Only by inner attendants placed Hall of Union and Peace three days.
translations.idiomatic: Only in her case were they placed in the Hall of Union and Peace for three days by inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 七年，定郊祀致齋，帝宿大內二日，壇內齋宮一日。

translations.literal: Year 7, fixed suburban sacrifice fasting, emperor lodged inner palace two days, within altar fasting palace one day.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 suburban sacrifice fasting was fixed: the emperor lodged in the inner palace two days and in the altar fasting palace one day.

sentences.zh: 王公居府第，餘在公署，俱二日。

translations.literal: Princes and dukes dwelt at mansions, the rest at official quarters, all two days.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes kept fasting at their mansions and the rest at official quarters, all for two days.

sentences.zh: 赴壇外齋宿一日。

translations.literal: Went outside altar to fast overnight one day.
translations.idiomatic: They then spent one night fasting outside the altar precinct.

sentences.zh: 若遣官代祭，王公不與。

translations.literal: If dispatched officials substituted sacrifice, princes and dukes did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: If officials were dispatched to substitute for the sacrifice, princes and dukes did not take part.

sentences.zh: 祭太廟、社稷，王公百官齋所如前儀，俱三日。

translations.literal: Sacrificing Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain, princes and dukes hundred officials fasting quarters as former rite, all three days.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the altars of soil and grain, princes, dukes, and all officials kept fasting as in the former rite, all for three days.

sentences.zh: 祭日、月、帝王、先師、先農，王公齋二日，遣代則否。

translations.literal: Sacrificing sun, moon, emperors, Former Teacher, Former Agriculture, princes and dukes fast two days; if dispatched substitute then not.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices to the sun, moon, ancient emperors, the Former Teacher, and the Former Agriculture, princes and dukes fasted two days; if an envoy substituted, they did not.

sentences.zh: 後饗先蠶，齋二日，公主、福晉、命婦陪祀者，前二日致齋。

translations.literal: Empress sacrificing to Silkworm Goddess, fast two days; princesses, imperial consorts, titled ladies attending sacrifice, two days before fasted.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress sacrificed to the Silkworm Goddess she fasted two days; princesses, imperial consorts, and titled ladies who attended the sacrifice began fasting two days beforehand.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔郊祀、祈穀、大雩，祭日宣誓戒，陪祀者集午門行禮，符古者百官受戒遺意。

translations.literal: Year 12, decreed suburban sacrifice, Prayer for Grain, Great Rain Prayer, on sacrifice day proclaimed oath of admonition, attendant sacrificers gathered Meridian Gate performed rite, matching ancient hundred officials receiving admonition intent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 an edict required that for suburban sacrifice, Prayer for Grain, and Great Rain Prayer, on the day of sacrifice the oath of admonition be proclaimed and attendant sacrificers gather at the Meridian Gate to perform the rite, echoing the ancient intent of all officials receiving admonition.

sentences.zh: 既有司具儀上，行之。

translations.literal: Once responsible office prepared rites and submitted, carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Once the responsible offices had prepared the rites and submitted them, the practice was carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋罷。

translations.literal: Soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 惟嚴敕大臣齋宿公所，領侍衛內大臣等齋宿紫禁城，違則治罪。

translations.literal: Only strictly commanded great ministers fast overnight at public quarters, leading inner grand ministers of the guard and others fast overnight Forbidden City; violation then punished.
translations.idiomatic: Only a strict command remained that great ministers fast overnight at the public quarters and that the leading inner grand ministers of the guard and others fast overnight within the Forbidden City, with punishment for violations.

sentences.zh: 初，齋宮致齋鳴鼓角，十四年諭云：「齋者耳不聽樂，孔子曰：『三日齋，一日用之，猶恐不敬，二日伐鼓何居？

translations.literal: Initially, fasting palace fasting sounded drums and horns; year 14 instructed: "One who fasts, the ear does not hear music. Confucius said: 'Three days fasting, one day using it—still fearing not reverent; two days beating drums—what is that for?
translations.idiomatic: At first the fasting palace sounded drums and horns during the fast; in year 14 the throne said: "In fasting the ear must not hear music. Confucius said, 'Three days of fasting, one day to use it—still fearing it is not reverent; two days of drum-beating—what is that for?

sentences.zh: 』言不敢散其志也。

translations.literal: ' Meaning dare not scatter one's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: '—meaning that one must not scatter one's resolve.

sentences.zh: 吹角鼓鼙，以壯軍容，於義未協，不當用也。

translations.literal: Blowing horns and beating war drums to strengthen military appearance—in meaning not harmonious, should not be used."
translations.idiomatic: Blowing horns and beating war drums to stiffen military bearing was not in harmony with the meaning of fasting and should not be used."

sentences.zh: 」遂寢。

translations.literal: Then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was then discontinued.

sentences.zh: 十九年，敕群臣書制辭於版，前期三日，陳設公堂，俾有所警。

translations.literal: Year 19, commanded ministers write regulated text on board; three days beforehand displayed in public hall, so there would be warning.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 ministers were commanded to write the regulated text on boards; three days beforehand these were displayed in the public hall so that all would be admonished.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年，諭誡齋戒執事暨查齋監禮者，循舊章，肅祀典。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 13, instructed admonishing fasting ritual officers together with inspectors of fasting and supervisors of rites, follow old regulations, solemnize sacrifice canon.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 13 the throne admonished fasting ritual officers together with inspectors of fasting and supervisors of the rites to follow the old regulations and keep the sacrificial canon solemn.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，監國攝政王代行，帝宮內致齋，停進齋戒牌及銅人。

translations.literal: Beginning of Xuantong, regent prince acting for state, emperor within palace fasted, stopped presenting fasting tablets and bronze man.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign, when the regent prince acted for the state, the emperor fasted within the palace and the presentation of fasting tablets and the bronze figure was suspended.

sentences.zh: 祝版以木為之，圜丘、方澤方一尺五寸，徑八寸四分，厚三分。

translations.literal: Prayer boards made of wood; Circular Mound, Square Mound square one chi five cun, diameter eight cun four fen, thickness three fen.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer boards were made of wood; for the Circular Mound and Square Mound they were square, one foot five inches on a side, eight inches four tenths in diameter, and three tenths of an inch thick.

sentences.zh: 祈穀壇方一尺一寸，徑一尺，厚如之。

translations.literal: Prayer for Grain Altar square one chi one cun, diameter one chi, thickness like it.
translations.idiomatic: For the Prayer for Grain Altar they were square, one foot one inch on a side, one foot in diameter, with the same thickness.

sentences.zh: 太廟後殿方一尺二寸，徑八寸四分。

translations.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple rear hall square one chi two cun, diameter eight cun four fen.
translations.idiomatic: For the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple they were square, one foot two inches on a side and eight inches four tenths in diameter.

sentences.zh: 前殿方二尺，徑一尺一寸，厚並同徑。

translations.literal: Front hall square two chi, diameter one chi one cun, thickness all same as diameter.
translations.idiomatic: For the front hall they were square, two feet on a side and one foot one inch in diameter, with thickness equal to the diameter throughout.

sentences.zh: 常雩，日、月壇，社稷壇與太廟後殿同。

translations.literal: Regular Rain Prayer, sun and moon altars, soil-and-grain altar same as Imperial Ancestral Temple rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: For the Regular Rain Prayer and the sun and moon altars, and the soil-and-grain altar, the dimensions matched those of the Imperial Ancestral Temple rear hall.

sentences.zh: 中祀、群祀方徑各有差。

translations.literal: Middle sacrifice, mass sacrifice square and diameter each had differences.
translations.idiomatic: For middle and mass sacrifices the length and diameter of the boards each differed.

sentences.zh: 天壇青紙青緣硃書，地壇黃紙黃緣墨書，月壇、太廟、社稷白紙黃緣墨書，日壇硃紙硃書，群祀白紙墨書不加緣。

translations.literal: Heaven Altar green paper green border vermilion writing; Earth Altar yellow paper yellow border ink writing; moon altar, Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain white paper yellow border ink writing; sun altar vermilion paper vermilion writing; mass sacrifice white paper ink writing without adding border.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven Altar boards used green paper with green borders and vermilion script; Earth Altar boards used yellow paper with yellow borders and ink script; the moon altar, Imperial Ancestral Temple, and soil-and-grain altars used white paper with yellow borders and ink script; the sun altar used vermilion paper and vermilion script; mass sacrifices used white paper and ink script without borders.

sentences.zh: 太常司令祝版官先期褾飾，祀前二日昧爽送內閣，授中書書祝辭，大學士書御名，餘祀太常司自繕。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices ordered prayer-board officers beforehand mounted and decorated; two days before sacrifice before dawn sent to Grand Secretariat, entrusted Secretariat Drafters write prayer text, grand secretaries write imperial name; remaining sacrifices Court of Imperial Sacrifices itself copied.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices ordered prayer-board officers to mount and decorate the boards beforehand; two days before the sacrifice, before dawn, they were sent to the Grand Secretariat, where Secretariat drafters wrote the prayer text and grand secretaries wrote the imperial name; for other sacrifices the Court of Imperial Sacrifices copied them itself.

sentences.zh: 凡親祭，先二日太常卿奏請，前一日閱祝版。

translations.literal: Whenever personal sacrifice, two days before Court of Imperial Sacrifices director memorialized request; one day before reviewed prayer board.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor sacrificed in person, two days beforehand the Court of Imperial Sacrifices director memorialized a request, and one day before he reviewed the prayer board.

sentences.zh: 圜丘、祈穀、常雩御太和殿，方澤、太廟、社稷御中和殿。

translations.literal: Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, Regular Rain Prayer used Supreme Harmony Hall; Square Mound, Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain used Central Harmony Hall.
translations.idiomatic: For the Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, and Regular Rain Prayer he used the Hall of Supreme Harmony; for the Square Mound, Imperial Ancestral Temple, and soil-and-grain altars he used the Hall of Central Harmony.

sentences.zh: 祝案居正中少西，案設羊角鐙二，視版日，案左楹東置香亭，右楹西置奉版亭、奉玉帛香亭。

translations.literal: Prayer desk centered slightly west, desk set ram's-horn stirrups two; on prayer-board review day, desk left pillar east placed incense pavilion, right pillar west placed presentation-board pavilion, presentation jade-silk incense pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer desk stood at the center, slightly to the west, with two ram's-horn stirrups set on the desk; on the day of reviewing the prayer board, east of the left pillar an incense pavilion was placed and west of the right pillar pavilions for presenting the board and for presenting jade, silk, and incense.

sentences.zh: 屆時太常卿詣乾清門啟奏，帝出宮詣案前。

translations.literal: At the hour Court of Imperial Sacrifices director went Gate of Heavenly Purity announced, emperor left palace went to desk before.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed hour the Court of Imperial Sacrifices director went to the Gate of Heavenly Purity to announce, and the emperor left the palace and came before the desk.

sentences.zh: 閱畢，行一跪三拜禮。

translations.literal: Review finished, performed one kneel three prostrations rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the review was finished he performed the rite of one kneel and three prostrations.

sentences.zh: 贊禮郎徹褥，寺卿韜版，導帝至香亭前，拜跪如初禮。

translations.literal: Eulogizing ritual officer removed mat, temple director wrapped board, guided emperor to before incense pavilion, kneeled and prostrated as initial rite.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogizing ritual officer removed the mat, the temple director wrapped the board, and guided the emperor before the incense pavilion to kneel and prostrate as in the first rite.

sentences.zh: 司祝奉版薦黃亭送祭所，庋神庫。

translations.literal: Prayer officer presented board to yellow pavilion sent to sacrifice place, stored spirit repository.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer presented the board to the yellow pavilion, which conveyed it to the sacrifice site and then stored it in the spirit repository.

sentences.zh: 大祀遣代，停止祝版具奏。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice dispatched substitute, stopped prayer board memorial submission.
translations.idiomatic: When a great sacrifice was performed by a dispatched substitute, the prayer-board memorial and presentation were stopped.

sentences.zh: 中祀、群祀，寺官赴內閣徑請送祭所，不具奏。

translations.literal: Middle sacrifice, mass sacrifice, temple officers went Grand Secretariat directly requested sent to sacrifice place, no memorial submission.
translations.idiomatic: For middle and mass sacrifices temple officers went to the Grand Secretariat to request the boards directly and sent them to the sacrifice site without a memorial submission.

sentences.zh: 其視玉、帛、香如閱祝版儀。

translations.literal: Their inspecting jade, silk, incense like reviewing prayer board rite.
translations.idiomatic: The inspection of jade, silk, and incense followed the same rite as reviewing the prayer board.

sentences.zh: 祭服圜丘、祈穀、雩祀，先一日，帝御齋宮，龍袍袞服。

translations.literal: Sacrificial robes: Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, rain sacrifice, one day before emperor at fasting palace, dragon robe and coronation dress.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial vestments: for the Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, and rain sacrifices, on the day before, the emperor at the fasting palace wore dragon robe and coronation dress.

sentences.zh: 屆期天青禮服。

translations.literal: At the date sky-blue ritual robes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the rite he wore sky-blue ritual robes.

sentences.zh: 方澤禮服明黃色，餘祀亦如之。

translations.literal: Square Mound ritual robes bright yellow, remaining sacrifices also like it.
translations.idiomatic: For the Square Mound the ritual robes were bright yellow, and other sacrifices followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 惟朝日大紅，夕月玉色。

translations.literal: Only Morning Sun great red, Evening Moon jade color.
translations.idiomatic: Only Morning Sun used great red and Evening Moon jade white.

sentences.zh: 王公以下陪祀執事官咸朝服。

translations.literal: Princes and dukes down to attendant sacrificers and ritual officers all court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes down through attendant sacrificers and ritual officers all wore court dress.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年，定祀前閱祝版執事官服色制，南郊祈穀、常雩、歲暮祫祭、元旦、萬壽、告祭太廟，蟒袍補褂，罷朝服。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 9, fixed before sacrifice reviewing prayer board ritual officers robe colors: southern suburb Prayer for Grain, Regular Rain Prayer, year-end joint sacrifice, New Year's Day, Longevity, announcement sacrifice Imperial Ancestral Temple, python robe rank-badge jacket, abolished court dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 9 the colors and styles for ritual officers who reviewed the prayer board before sacrifice were fixed: for southern-suburb Prayer for Grain, Regular Rain Prayer, year-end joint sacrifice, New Year's Day, Longevity celebrations, and announcement sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple they wore python robes with rank-badge jackets instead of court dress.

sentences.zh: 社稷、時享太廟，服補服。

translations.literal: Soil and grain, seasonal offering Imperial Ancestral Temple, wore rank-badge robe.
translations.idiomatic: For the soil-and-grain altars and seasonal offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple they wore rank-badge robes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，諭郊壇大祀若遇國忌，仍御禮服，禮成還宮更素服。

translations.literal: Year 11, instructed suburban altar great sacrifice if encountering state mourning, still wore ritual robes; rite finished returning palace changed plain robes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the throne instructed that if a suburban altar great sacrifice fell on a day of state mourning the emperor still wore ritual robes and changed to plain robes only after the rite when he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十九年，諭郊祀遇國忌，前一日閱祝版，帝服龍袍龍褂，執事官蟒袍補服。

translations.literal: Year 19, instructed suburban sacrifice encountering state mourning, one day before reviewing prayer board, emperor wore dragon robe dragon jacket, ritual officers python robe rank-badge jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 it was instructed that when a suburban sacrifice fell on state mourning, on the day before reviewing the prayer board the emperor wore dragon robe and dragon jacket and ritual officers wore python robes with rank-badge jackets.

sentences.zh: 大祀、中祀，帝龍褂，執事官補服。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice, middle sacrifice, emperor dragon jacket, ritual officers rank-badge robe.
translations.idiomatic: For great and middle sacrifices the emperor wore a dragon jacket and ritual officers rank-badge robes.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: Established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This was established as a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，定制大祀齋期遇國忌，悉改常服。

translations.literal: Year 23, fixed regulation great sacrifice fasting period encountering state mourning, all changed to regular robes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 a regulation was fixed that during the fasting period for a great sacrifice that fell on state mourning all changed to regular robes.

sentences.zh: 中祀則限於承祭官及陪祀、執事官，餘素服如故。

translations.literal: Middle sacrifice then limited to presiding sacrificer and attendant sacrificers, ritual officers; the rest plain robes as before.
translations.idiomatic: For middle sacrifices the rule applied only to the presiding sacrificer, attendant sacrificers, and ritual officers; everyone else remained in plain robes as before.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，諭大祀親祭或遣官致祭遇國忌，齋期一依向例，中祀親祭同。

translations.literal: Year 25, instructed great sacrifice personal sacrifice or dispatched official performing sacrifice encountering state mourning, fasting period all follow former precedent; middle sacrifice personal sacrifice same.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 it was instructed that when a great sacrifice performed in person or by a dispatched official fell on state mourning, the fasting-period dress followed the former precedent, and the same held for a middle sacrifice performed in person.

sentences.zh: 其遣官致祭，與執事、陪祀官常服掛珠，否則仍素服。

translations.literal: If dispatched official performing sacrifice, together with ritual, attendant sacrificers regular robes with prayer beads hung, otherwise still plain robes.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice was performed by a dispatched official, he together with ritual and attendant sacrificers wore regular robes with prayer beads; otherwise they still wore plain robes.

sentences.zh: 祭告凡登極授受大典，上尊號、徽號，祔廟，郊祀，萬壽節，皇太后萬壽節，冊立皇太子，先期遣官祗告天地、太廟、社稷。

translations.literal: Sacrifice announcements: whenever ascending throne transmission-of-mandate great ceremony, bestowing honorific title, honorific epithet, enshrining in temple, suburban sacrifice, Longevity Festival, empress dowager Longevity Festival, investing crown prince—beforehand dispatched officials reverently announced Heaven and Earth, Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial announcements: whenever the emperor acceded to the throne, received the transmission-of-mandate ceremony, bestowed honorific titles or epithets, enshrined an ancestor, performed a suburban sacrifice, celebrated the Longevity Festival or the empress dowager's Longevity Festival, or invested the crown prince, officials were dispatched beforehand to reverently announce the rite to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 致祭岳鎮、海瀆、帝王陵寢、先師闕里、先師。

translations.literal: Also sacrificed at Five Sacred Peaks, four seas, imperial tombs, Former Teacher at Queli, Former Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: They also sacrificed at the Five Sacred Peaks, the four seas, imperial tombs, the Former Teacher at Queli, and the Former Teacher.

sentences.zh: 改大祀亦如之。

translations.literal: Changed to great sacrifice also like it.
translations.idiomatic: When a rite was raised to great-sacrifice status the same rule applied.

sentences.zh: 大婚冊立皇后，祗告天地、太廟。

translations.literal: Great wedding investing empress, reverently announced Heaven and Earth, Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: For a grand wedding and the investiture of an empress they reverently announced Heaven and Earth and the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 尊封太妃、冊封皇貴妃及貴妃，祗告太廟後殿奉先殿。

translations.literal: Honoring consort dowager, investing imperial noble consort and noble consort, reverently announced Imperial Ancestral Temple rear hall Hall of Ancestral Worship.
