translations.idiomatic: When honoring a consort dowager or investing an imperial noble consort or noble consort they reverently announced the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Hall of Ancestral Worship.

sentences.zh: 追上尊諡廟號、葬陵，祗告天地、社稷、太廟後殿、奉先殿，並致祭陵寢、后土、陵山。

translations.literal: Posthumously bestowing honorific epithet temple name, burying at mausoleum, reverently announced Heaven and Earth, soil and grain, Imperial Ancestral Temple rear hall, Hall of Ancestral Worship, and also sacrificed at mausoleum, Queen of Earth, mausoleum mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When posthumously bestowing an honorific epithet and temple name or burying at a mausoleum they reverently announced Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Hall of Ancestral Worship, and also sacrificed at the mausoleum, the Queen of Earth, and the mausoleum mountain.

sentences.zh: 親征命將，祗告天地，太廟，社稷，太歲，火砲、道路諸神。

translations.literal: Personally campaigning commissioning generals, reverently announced Heaven and Earth, Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain, Grand Year, cannon, road various spirits.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally took the field or commissioned generals they reverently announced Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the altars of soil and grain, the Grand Year star, and the spirits of cannon and roads.

sentences.zh: 凱旋奏功，祗告奉先殿，致祭陵寢，釋奠先師，致祭岳鎮、海瀆、帝王陵廟、先師闕里。

translations.literal: Triumphant return presenting merit, reverently announced Hall of Ancestral Worship, sacrificed at mausoleum, released libation Former Teacher, sacrificed at Five Sacred Peaks, four seas, imperial tombs and temples, Former Teacher at Queli.
translations.idiomatic: On triumphant return when presenting merit they reverently announced the Hall of Ancestral Worship, sacrificed at the mausoleum, released a libation to the Former Teacher, and sacrificed at the Five Sacred Peaks, the four seas, imperial tombs and temples, and the Former Teacher at Queli.

sentences.zh: 謁陵、巡狩，並祗告奉先殿，迴鑾亦如之。

translations.literal: Visiting mausoleum, imperial tour, all reverently announced Hall of Ancestral Worship; returning imperial carriage also like it.
translations.idiomatic: When visiting a mausoleum or making an imperial tour they all reverently announced the Hall of Ancestral Worship, and the same when the imperial carriage returned.

sentences.zh: 巡幸所蒞，親祭方岳。

translations.literal: Touring to places arrived at, personally sacrificed at regional peaks.
translations.idiomatic: At places the tour actually reached, the emperor personally sacrificed at the regional peaks.

sentences.zh: 其所未蒞者，命疆臣選員遍祭岳、鎮、海、瀆、所過名山大川。

translations.literal: Those not yet arrived at, commanded border officials select officers everywhere sacrifice peaks, passes, seas, estuaries, famous mountains and great rivers passed along the way.
translations.idiomatic: Where he had not yet arrived, border officials were commanded to select officers to sacrifice everywhere at the peaks, passes, seas, estuaries, and famous mountains and great rivers along the route.

sentences.zh: 其祭文香帛，遣使自京齎送。

translations.literal: Their sacrificial texts, incense, and silk, dispatched envoys from capital carried and sent.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial texts, incense, and silk were carried from the capital by dispatched envoys.

sentences.zh: 帝王陵寢、聖賢忠烈暨名臣祠墓，凡在三十里內，遣官祭之。

translations.literal: Imperial tombs, sages loyal and valiant together with famous ministers' shrines and tombs, all within thirty li, dispatched officials sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: For imperial tombs and the shrines and tombs of sages, the loyal and valiant, and famous ministers, whenever these lay within thirty li officials were dispatched to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 歲暮祫祭，功臣配饗，祗告太廟中殿、後殿。

translations.literal: Year-end joint sacrifice, meritorious subjects paired offerings, reverently announced Imperial Ancestral Temple central hall, rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: For the year-end joint sacrifice and the paired offerings to meritorious subjects, they reverently announced the central and rear halls of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 監國攝政，並遣官祭告太廟。

translations.literal: Supervising state regency, also dispatched officials sacrifice-announce Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When supervising the state or serving as regent, officials were also dispatched to announce sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 耕耤田，祗告奉先殿。

translations.literal: Plowing Furrow Field, reverently announced Hall of Ancestral Worship.
translations.idiomatic: When plowing the Furrow Field they reverently announced the Hall of Ancestral Worship.

sentences.zh: 御經筵，祗告奉先殿、傳心殿，修建郊壇、太廟、奉先殿，祗告天地、太廟、社稷。

translations.literal: Holding classics lecture, reverently announced Hall of Ancestral Worship, Hall of Transmitting the Heart; constructing suburban altar, Imperial Ancestral Temple, Hall of Ancestral Worship, reverently announced Heaven and Earth, Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When holding the classics lecture they reverently announced the Hall of Ancestral Worship and the Hall of Transmitting the Heart; when constructing the suburban altar, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, or the Hall of Ancestral Worship they reverently announced Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 興工、合龍，祭后土、司工諸神。

translations.literal: Commencing work, joining dragon, sacrificed Queen of Earth, Superintendent of Works various spirits.
translations.idiomatic: When work commenced or the embankments were joined they sacrificed to the Queen of Earth and the various spirits of the Superintendent of Works.

sentences.zh: 迎吻，祭琉璃窯神暨各門神。

translations.literal: Receiving roof-ridge finial, sacrificed glazed-tile kiln spirit together with each gate spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When the roof-ridge finial was installed they sacrificed to the spirit of the glazed-tile kiln and to each gate spirit.

sentences.zh: 歲旱祈雨，祗告天神、地祇、太歲。

translations.literal: Year drought praying rain, reverently announced heavenly spirits, earthly spirits, Grand Year.
translations.idiomatic: In years of drought when praying for rain they reverently announced the heavenly spirits, earthly spirits, and the Grand Year star.

sentences.zh: 越七日，祭告社稷。

translations.literal: Passing seven days, sacrifice-announced soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: After seven days they announced sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 三請不雨，始行大雩。

translations.literal: Three petitions without rain, then began performing Great Rain Prayer.
translations.idiomatic: If three petitions brought no rain, the Great Rain Prayer ceremony was then performed.

sentences.zh: 凡告祀，不及配位從壇。

translations.literal: All announcement sacrifices, did not reach paired positions attendant altars.
translations.idiomatic: For all announcement sacrifices, ancillary paired positions and attendant altars were not included.

sentences.zh: 至為元元祈福，則遣大臣分行祭告，頒冊文香帛，給御蓋一，龍纛御仗各二，蓋猶喬嶽翕河茂典雲。

translations.literal: Reaching praying blessing for myriad people, then dispatched great ministers in branches sacrifice-announce, distributed patent texts incense silk, granted imperial canopy one, dragon banners imperial staffs each two, canopy still lofty peaks converging rivers flourishing ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When praying for the blessing of the myriad people, great ministers were dispatched in separate parties to announce sacrifice, patent texts and incense and silk were distributed, and one imperial canopy was granted together with two dragon banners and two imperial staffs apiece—still in the elevated ceremonial precedent of lofty peaks and converging rivers.

sentences.zh: 習儀凡大祀前四十日，中祀前三十日，每旬三、六、九日，太常卿帥讀祝官、贊禮郎暨執事、樂舞集神樂署，習儀凝禧殿。

translations.literal: Rehearsal rites: all great sacrifices forty days before, middle sacrifices thirty days before, each ten-day period third sixth ninth days, Director of Ceremonies led prayer-reading officers, praise officers together with ritual officers, music and dance gathered Imperial Music Office, rehearsed rites Hall of Condensed Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Rehearsal rites: for great sacrifices forty days beforehand and middle sacrifices thirty days beforehand, on the third, sixth, and ninth of each ten-day period the Director of Ceremonies led prayer-reading officers, praise officers, ritual officers, and musicians and dancers to gather at the Imperial Music Office and rehearse at the Hall of Condensed Blessings.

sentences.zh: 故事，祭祀先期，太常寺演禮壇廟中。

translations.literal: Precedent: sacrifices beforehand, Court of Imperial Sacrifices rehearsed rites within altar temples.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, before sacrifices the Court of Imperial Sacrifices rehearsed the rites at the altar temples.

sentences.zh: 雍正九年諭曰：「是雖義取嫻熟，實乖潔齊嚴肅本旨也。

translations.literal: Yongzheng year 9 instructed saying: "This although meaning takes practiced fluency, truly violates purification order solemn gravity fundamental aim.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 9 an edict said: "Although this takes its meaning from practiced fluency, it truly violates the fundamental aim of purification, order, solemnity, and gravity.

sentences.zh: 」乃停前一日壇廟演禮。

translations.literal: " Then stopped one day before altar-temple rehearsed rites.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore rehearsal at the altars and temples the day before was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 其前二日凝禧殿如故。

translations.literal: Its two days before Hall of Condensed Blessings as before.
translations.idiomatic: The rehearsal two days beforehand at the Hall of Condensed Blessings remained as before.

sentences.zh: 饗太廟，以王公一人監視宗室、覺羅官。

translations.literal: Feasting Imperial Ancestral Temple, with one prince of the blood supervised imperial clansmen, gioro officials.
translations.idiomatic: For feasting at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, one prince of the blood supervised the imperial clansmen and gioro officials.

sentences.zh: 祀先師，祭酒、司業監視國子師生，同日習樂殿庭，令樂部典樂監視亦如之。

translations.literal: Sacrificing Former Teacher, Chancellor Vice-Chancellor supervised National University teachers students, same day rehearsed music hall courtyard, ordered Music Bureau Director of Music supervised likewise.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrificing to the Former Teacher, the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor supervised National University teachers and students; on the same day music was rehearsed in the hall courtyard, and the Director of Music of the Music Bureau was ordered to supervise in the same way.

sentences.zh: 謁陵寢，讀祝官等亦遇三、六、九日習儀皇陵。

translations.literal: Visiting mausoleum, prayer-reading officers etc also encountering third sixth ninth days rehearsed rites at imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When visiting a mausoleum, prayer-reading officers and the like also rehearsed at the imperial tombs on the third, sixth, and ninth days.

sentences.zh: 又歲暮將祭享，選內大臣打莽式，例演習於禮曹。

translations.literal: Also year-end about to sacrifice and feast, selected inner grand councillors performed mang-style, precedent rehearsed at Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Also at year-end, before the sacrificial feasts, inner grand councillors were selected to perform the mang-style dance, which by precedent was rehearsed at the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時議謂發揚蹈厲，為公庭萬舞變態雲。

translations.literal: Contemporary discussion said displaying vigor treading forcefully, was court myriad dances transformed form.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary discussion held that its vigorous display and forceful treading were a transformation of the court's myriad dances.

sentences.zh: 陪祀順治時，詔陪祀官視加級四品以上。

translations.literal: Attendant sacrifice Shunzhi era, decreed attendant sacrificers regarded as added-grade fourth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: For attendant sacrifice in the Shunzhi era, an edict treated attendant sacrificers as officials of added-grade fourth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十五年，以喧語失儀，諭誡陪祀官毋慢易。

translations.literal: Kangxi year 25, because clamor speech lost decorum, instructed admonished attendant sacrificers not negligent.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25, because clamorous speech caused a breach of decorum, attendant sacrificers were instructed and admonished not to be negligent.

sentences.zh: 尋議定論職不論級。

translations.literal: Soon deliberated fixed: discuss office, not discuss rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward it was deliberated and fixed that office, not rank, should govern.

sentences.zh: 郊壇陪祀，首公，訖阿達哈哈番，佐領。

translations.literal: Suburban altar attendant sacrifice, first duke, ending ada hahafan, assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For suburban altar attendant sacrifice the order ran from duke down to ada hahafan and assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 文官首尚書，訖員外郎，滿科道，漢掌印給事中。

translations.literal: Civil officials first Minister, ending vice director, Manchu censorate circuit, Han sealed memorial presenting censor.
translations.idiomatic: Among civil officials the order ran from minister down to vice director, Manchu censorate circuit intendant, and Han sealed-memorial presenting censor.

sentences.zh: 武訖游擊。

translations.literal: Military ending battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Among military officials it ended at battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 祭太廟、社稷、日月、帝王廟，武至參領，文至郎中，餘如前例。

translations.literal: Sacrificing Imperial Ancestral Temple, soil and grain, sun and moon, emperors' temple, military to deputy commandant, civil to director, rest as former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the altars of soil and grain, the sun and moon, and the Temple of Emperors, military officials went down to deputy commandant and civil officials to director; the rest followed the former precedent.

sentences.zh: 御史、禮曹並糾其失儀者。

translations.literal: Censors, Ministry of Rites together corrected those losing decorum.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and the Ministry of Rites together corrected those who lost decorum.

sentences.zh: 既以浙江提督陳世凱請，文廟春秋致祭，允武官二品以上陪祀。

translations.literal: Already because Zhejiang Provincial Commander Chen Shikai requested, Confucian temple spring autumn sacrifices, permitted military officials second rank and above attendant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhejiang provincial commander Chen Shikai memorialized, for spring and autumn sacrifices at the Confucian temple military officials of second rank and above were permitted to attend as sacrificers.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，申定陪祀不到者處分。

translations.literal: Year 39, reaffirmed fixed attendant sacrificers not arriving penalties.
translations.idiomatic: In year 39 penalties were reaffirmed for attendant sacrificers who failed to arrive.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初元，定陪祀祗候例，祭太廟，俟午門鳴鼓；

translations.literal: Qianlong first year, fixed attendant sacrifice reverent waiting precedent, sacrificing Imperial Ancestral Temple, waited Meridian Gate drum sounded;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong the precedent for reverent waiting by attendant sacrificers was fixed: for sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple they waited until the Meridian Gate drum sounded;

sentences.zh: 祭社稷，俟午門鳴鐘；

translations.literal: Sacrificing soil and grain, waited Meridian Gate bell sounded;
translations.idiomatic: for sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain they waited until the Meridian Gate bell sounded;

sentences.zh: 祭各壇廟，俟齋宮鍾動：依次入，鵠立，禁先登階。

translations.literal: Sacrificing each altar temple, waited fasting palace bell moved: entered in order, stood erect like swans, forbade first ascending steps.
translations.idiomatic: for sacrifice at each altar and temple they waited until the fasting-palace bell sounded: they entered in order, stood erect like swans, and were forbidden to ascend the steps first.

sentences.zh: 並按官品制木牌，肅班序。

translations.literal: Also according to official rank made wooden placards, arranged ranks in order.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden placards were also made according to official rank to arrange the ranks in proper order.

sentences.zh: 七年，定郊廟、社稷赴壇陪祀制，遣官代行，王公內大臣等不陪祀，餘如故。

translations.literal: Year 7, fixed suburban altars, soil and grain going to altar attendant sacrifice system, dispatched officials acted in place, princes inner grand councillors etc not attendant sacrifice, rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 the system for attendant sacrificers going to the altar at suburban altars and the altars of soil and grain was fixed so that dispatched officials acted in their place and princes, inner grand councillors, and the like no longer attended as sacrificers; the rest remained as before.

sentences.zh: 明年，定郊祭前一日申、酉時及祭日五鼓，禮部、察院官赴壇外受職名，餘祀止當日收受。

translations.literal: Next year, fixed suburban sacrifice one day before shen you hours and sacrifice day fifth drum, Ministry of Rites, Censorate officials went outside altar received duty names, other sacrifices only same day received.
translations.idiomatic: The next year it was fixed that for suburban sacrifice, on the day before at the shen and you hours and on the sacrifice day at the fifth drum, Ministry of Rites and Censorate officials went outside the altar to receive duty names; for other sacrifices names were received only on the day itself.

sentences.zh: 二十七年歲杪，諭通覈陪祀逾三次不到者，分別議懲。

translations.literal: Year 27 year-end, instructed comprehensive check attendant sacrificers exceeding three times not arriving, differentiated deliberate penalties.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of year 27 an edict ordered a comprehensive review of attendant sacrificers who had failed to arrive more than three times, with differentiated penalties to be deliberated.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，諭朝日陪祀無故不到或臨時稱疾，並處罰。

translations.literal: Xianfeng year 10, instructed morning audience attendant sacrifice without cause not arriving or temporarily claiming illness, all punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 an edict required that attendant sacrificers at the morning audience who failed to arrive without cause or who claimed illness at the last moment should all be punished.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，申定祗候例，大祀夜分、中祀雞初鳴，朝服蒞祭所。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 9, reaffirmed fixed reverent waiting precedent, great sacrifice midnight division, middle sacrifice cock first crow, court robes arrived sacrifice place.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 the precedent for reverent waiting was reaffirmed: for great sacrifices at midnight, for middle sacrifices at the cock's first crow, attendant sacrificers arrived at the sacrifice ground in court robes.
